# Bounded workload pooling implementation

Baseline: `e4d707de5634a8d758c606b4432037e1a1682052`. Design:
[WORKLOAD_SCHEDULING.md](WORKLOAD_SCHEDULING.md). Branch:
`codex/workload-scheduling` (PR #849).

## Canonical prepared replay key plans (2026-10-20)

Source `4c8ab4ee1a7143dc0e06b1e887475e7b0cb5afb7` derives replay wire costs and owned physical document-prefix
roots from the canonical prepared request batch and all seven accepted-effect
families. The request walker classifies every DerivedBatch field; the accepted
walker classifies every PrecomputedGeneratedBatch field. Compile-time field
coverage and an exhaustive document-action switch require an explicit decision
when either contract grows. Upserts, document deletes and preserved base documents
have separate contributions. Preserved base documents alone do not add an upsert key to the
estimate; this planner does not change replay notification semantics.

The estimate includes explicit artifact tombstones in both deletion/artifact
lanes, graph owner/source/target wake-ups, generated documents outside the request,
vector artifact owners and parents, deferred enrichment references and coverage
roots. Alias roots share one encoded-prefix identity. A mixed deletion lane can
contain a public binary ID that looks like a physical artifact: the conservative
plan retains both possible owners rather than guessing. Costs may overestimate
canonical deduplication and roots need not be minimal. Existing retirement costs
still come from the durable credit owner's known physical inventory.

Normal DocStore transactions, batches and batch adapters now have an internal
reservePreparedReplayPlan entry. It checks the original lifetime and file reader
eligibility before looking up frame payloads, decodes the exact stored frame
against the expected full transaction/catalog/schema contract, derives the key
plan, and reserves through the existing atomic HA credit primitive. The decoded
frame and temporary root plan have explicit cleanup owners; failed work poisons
the writer. No scalar base estimate or manually selected root list is accepted by
this entry. Existing lower-level credit APIs remain internal primitives.

The 78-step native run passes 66 executions: ten new plan
cases, ten existing credit cases and 46 encoder/boundary cases, with zero skips,
failures or leaks. New cases compare against actual thin and materialized request
builders and canonical CJ2 encoding, exercise every accepted family, cover absent
graph tombstones and binary ID ambiguity, exhaust allocation failures, preserve
original rejection, reject mismatched frame contracts and block disabled files
before payload lookup. A real writer reserves generated roots outside the request,
saturates the publication pool, and materializes/acknowledges its exactly bounded
record without another retention grant.

`prepared-replay-plan-verified.json` binds 5286 native/schema
inputs and 4559 matching immutable public sources.
The unchanged consumer main/build pass 25/25 ReleaseSafe composition steps. Its
cache workspace was recreated after GC; checked-in consumer bodies were preserved.
This is not provider-image, full archive-product or cold-source runtime
qualification. Private ABI versions, reader floors and durable wire formats are
unchanged; full Linux qualification remains waived.

This plan is complete for the supplied canonical preparation inputs, not yet a
certificate that those inputs are the real transaction. The driver must derive
and bind that prepared request to the authoritative intent/catalog witness and
include every auxiliary physical and replay effect, including grouped-source
changes, before sealing a vote. That provenance
check is not inferred from a matching accepted-effects frame alone. Derived-log
quota, minimum executable RAM/CPU/I/O/dependency recovery ownership, restart debt
reconstruction, confirmed-abort authority, legacy/import/raw migration rules and
normal PREPARE orchestration still need integration. Strong required providers
remain disabled; broader scheduler/default rollout and the full goal are open.

## Durable HA replay retention and atomic inventory credit (2026-10-20)

Source `28afa047da9b0f97af35f9e5bdc80c866bc02c38` adds internal DocStore writer primitives for durable HA replay
retention. A grant binds one transaction ID, the exact stored prepared-effects
frame fingerprint, an immutable caller-supplied base shape and a sorted set of
physical document-prefix hashes. Codec inspection checks the frame's transaction
identity before installation. Per-document claims retain known physical inventory;
unknown or invalidated inventory cannot become a zero estimate. Conflicting
owners, changed plan identities and impossible wire shapes fail before publication.

The existing logical publication pool reserves the CJ2 wire bound, fixed grant
record and both grant/outbox keys. Claim and owner-index rows charge their own
retained keys and values. Normal transactions, batches and append writers stage
physical inventory, claim totals, the grant and publication debt in one atomic
commit under the shared mutation gate. Final deltas admit replacement regardless
of insertion/deletion order. Saturated growth leaves physical data, inventory and
debt unchanged. Raw grant changes cannot replace the accepted base/roots/frame;
only trusted inventory staging can adjust its current-inventory contribution.
Ignored reservation or obligation failures poison the writer.

Materialization validates the supplied CJ2 bytes against existing credit, releases
inventory claims and retains the original reservation until explicit HA replay
acknowledgement. Repeated identical payloads are idempotent; a different payload
cannot replace the first. Ordinary frame cleanup cannot forgive replay debt.
Prepared credit cannot be acknowledged, and materialized credit cannot be canceled.
Cancellation is an internal primitive for a future participant driver to bind to
a confirmed abort; phase alone does not prove that no COMMIT decision exists.
Final writer-view validation uses fixed metadata and key presence rather than
rereading cold frame or replay values. Tests cover both possible outcomes of an
uncertain materialization commit and native reopen through all three phases.

The primitive requires both reader floor and permanent replacement baseline 11.
First use installs a permanent protocol marker that prevents later floor deletion
or lowering through DocStore, including after all grants drain. There is no new
full-protocol activation or legacy migration API. Native ABI 52, API ABI 58 and
storage-owner ABI 110 fence older private owners; runnable ABI 18 and failure ABI
66 are unchanged. Existing required-preparation reader version remains 10.

`durable-replay-credit-verified.json` binds 5285 native/schema
inputs, 4558 matching immutable public sources and
25/25 ReleaseSafe unchanged-consumer build steps. Six focused suites cover
163 successful test executions, including ten new credit
cases, with zero skips, failures or leaks in their qualifying results. Five suites
passed in the combined run; its required-DB suite exposed stale version/provider
fixtures. After changing only six named fixture bodies, all 22 required-DB cases
passed on rerun. The verifier proves every production byte and every other test
body stayed identical across that correction; it preserves the failed receipt
and does not claim a single all-green combined invocation. Consumer evidence is
module composition, not full archive products or cold-source runtime. Full Linux
qualification remains waived.

This does not yet fund a complete accepted transaction. The caller's base shape
and affected root set still need derivation and completeness checks from the full
request and accepted generated effects. Legacy transactions without grants retain
their original resolution policy, so legacy replay debt has no new complete bound.
Derived-log quota, backend working RAM/CPU/I/O/dependency recovery bundles, restart
reconstruction before ordinary admission, peer/import/raw migration eligibility,
and normal PREPARE/seal/abort driver integration remain required. Strong required
providers remain disabled. Broader scheduling, default rollout and whole-design
qualification remain incomplete.

## Inventory-backed retirement wire bounds (2026-10-20)

Source `65194cc0a474e11f500a5b7c64737322de64f69e` adds a low-level canonical CJ2 shape model and uses it
in the live encoder's exact sizing pass. Each present list costs its four-byte
count, four bytes per key length and the key bytes; one record costs a 16-byte
header including the hint mask. Shape merges combine list totals without
repeating headers. Counts, lengths and sums reject wire-limit overflow before
allocation. Existing CJ2 bytes and all private/durable ABI versions are unchanged.

For known physical inventory with `N` keys and `B` key bytes, retirement can
conservatively contribute these list totals:

| List | Key count bound | Key bytes bound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changed documents | `3N` | `B` |
| Deleted documents | `N` | `B` |
| Changed artifacts | `N` | `B` |

Thin replay copies removal
keys into both deletion and artifact lanes. Materialized graph removals can also
name owner/source/target; their distinct decoded bytes fit in the encoded
relationship keys, with aliases deduplicated by the canonical builders. Charging
all physical families for these lanes conservatively includes non-graph keys.
For representable nonempty inventory the wire bound is `28 + 20*N + 3*B`; an empty shape costs
16 bytes. Request effects, new generated effects and persistence envelope/key
charges must be added separately. Missing or invalidated inventory remains
unknown and must be reconciled before a prepare can rely on it.

The 69-step focused run passes 45 wire cases plus a boundary companion and
14 inventory cases. A real DB deletion covers escaped owner/source/target IDs,
legacy and explicit graph relationships, asset/chunk/vector artifacts, unchanged
inventory on value replacement, physical removal and endpoint notifications.
The same fact bounds explicit thin and materialized encoder inputs. Fixture
seeding publishes the normal owner's artifact-presence marker before deletion;
raw physical writes alone do not refresh the DB's cached presence witness.
Checked overflow and additive growth tests accompany existing inventory lifecycle
and byte-for-byte wire checks.

`inventory-replay-shape-verified.json` binds 5270 native inputs,
4552 matching immutable public sources and 25/25 ReleaseSafe
consumer build steps. The public consumer checks module composition only; full
archive/cold-source runtime remain unqualified and the full Linux sweep is waived.
This is a wire-cost calculation, not durable credit or working RAM/CPU/I/O
ownership. Durable reservations before PREPARE, atomic background credit RMW,
minimum recovery bundles, required-provider orchestration and remaining broader
scheduling integration remain unfinished. Required-mode providers remain disabled
and the full design remains incomplete.

## Replay decoder validation before allocation (2026-10-20)

Source `5e48b391853a4a1069ce0370b5de70c88d531bff` validates the complete CJ2 envelope before owned, borrowed
or selected scratch decoders allocate from wire counts. Impossible counts,
truncation in any field, trailing bytes and reserved field flags reject before
hint or key descriptor allocation. Valid CJ2 bytes and decoded values remain
unchanged. The allocation-free inspection reports encoded input bytes, per-list
key counts/bytes and hint count. Its checked sizing methods measure exact owned
or borrowed allocation payload bytes; they exclude allocator headers/alignment,
input storage and ArrayList spare capacity. Inspection can poll original controls
every 64 entries while skipping key contents. Existing decode/copy loops remain
synchronous; this is not a new cooperative decode or durable completion grant.

147 replay-allocation cases and the 43-case wire suite (these suites overlap),
plus their root/boundary companions. All 4096 field/hint combinations compare
actual owned/borrowed allocation payloads with inspection. Every truncation of a
multi-field fixture, forged counts, trailing data and reserved flags rejects with
a refusing allocator without attempting allocation. Original inspection control
rejection propagates at each metadata checkpoint.

code before its test section is unchanged; production limits are not relaxed.

## Original-scope checks during producer CPU admission (2026-10-20)

Source `c7de4b1b80ee26ce2643229f7cc39e6aaef21dbf` adds checked child activation to the native scheduler,
owner port and borrowed child bridge. The original call-scoped restriction is
polled before queueing, during bounded CPU waiting and after a grant, outside
the scheduler lock. Retired-holder producer preparation uses this capability.
A stricter deadline or fallible authority can reject a queued producer while a
peer still holds the only ordinary CPU. Refusal releases runnable capacity but
retains child metadata, operation ownership and parent linkage until owning
finish. The borrowed bridge preserves the first private failure across status
aliases and repeated activation/lifetime checks. Checked activation never falls
back to an unchecked callback.

## Independent CPU for retired-holder producer work (2026-10-20)

Source `97e121f317cb2c742730edd30e243a2d48ef9809` reserves a distinct producer
child from the original execution after owned policy and capture holders retire.
The parent parks before the child activates. The child inherits the original
request's scheduler, deadline, cancellation, class and queue restrictions; it
uses the borrowed request IO and bounded child-metadata allocator. Provider
invocations and their internal consumers return/join before child retirement.
Original parent CPU reenters through a checked restriction before holders are
restored. A failed speculative call retires the child and leaves parent cleanup
to its owning finish, without renewing foreground authority.

The write completion adapter supplies a separate producer parent for this
retired-holder phase. Its ordinary parking callbacks still reject use before
completion activates; producer work does not activate completion. A live producer
prevents holder reentry. Providers receive only the independently admitted child,
never the coordinator token. Scoped dense/sparse contexts and nested asset
invocations preserve it; the shared lifecycle runtime stays unchanged. Asset
invocation planning and dispatch treat a runnable as controlled authority.
Provider fanout and PDF prefetch remain disabled for scoped preparation.

Native ABI 50, runnable ABI 17 and API ABI 56 fence the changed process-local
layouts and producer-parent callback. Storage-owner 109, failure 66, engine
descriptor 29, reader floor 10 and durable formats remain unchanged.

`independent-producer-execution-v6` passes 81/81 focused build steps, with
46 provider/admission cases, 21 PDF/funding cases and 16 write-team cases.
Seven owner-preflight cases plus their root retain unchanged-source passing
provenance from v5; only the write-team test's required license header changed.
The actual DB fixture covers document/relational dense, sparse and two-asset
consumers, with one ordinary CPU slot and a separate control slot. It checks
parked parent ownership, child-only execution, query/control progress during
child parking, inherited deadlines, cancellation, reservation refusal, rejected
parent reentry and no row commit on failure. The real write-team adapter checks
bounded metadata retirement and that completion stays inactive. Asset-runtime
checks preserve the child token without changing the resident runtime.

`independent-producer-verified.json` binds 5267 unchanged native inputs and
4549 matching immutable public sources, with 25/25 ReleaseSafe public-consumer
build steps. The consumer checks module composition without linking provider
products. Source-controller coverage remains semantic; the small linked
visibility fixture proves its contract only. Full archive/cold-source runtime
remain unqualified, and full Linux qualification remains waived.

Legacy capabilities, already granted whole teams, externally retained snapshot
or policy holders and in-apply fallback retain their existing CPU path. Complete
producer eligibility and independently funded parallel children remain open.
Durable accepted effects and completion reservations before PREPARE, required-mode
provider activation/readiness, hidden-owner authority, remaining routes/backends,
overload faults and default-policy integration remain unfinished. The full
design remains incomplete; this does not activate required-mode providers.

## Speculative producer holder retirement (2026-10-20)

Source `decfefff899c926b0ac7ccb3a07ac2ca6118d65f`: eligible controlled document and relational precompute now retire their owned
policy admission and both nested and enclosing capture readers before provider
work. This phase precedes snapshot mutation and exclusive apply admission. The
same capture root and original controls stay attached to the retirement scope.
Capture reentry does not wait while caller CPU is held, and partial admissions
retire on failure. Another live root borrower prevents retirement.

Policy reentry restores the original write lease only when phase, policy
generation, catalog epoch and schema version still match. Both authentication
expiry domains remain unchanged; reentry never authenticates anew or makes a
fresh deadline. A failed reentry consumes its guard. Existing apply-time catalog
and row-observation validation still decides whether the computed effects can
be committed. No shared admission layout, status number or durable format changes.

The caller still retains CPU through this speculative phase. External snapshot
holders, borrowed policy holders and the in-apply generated fallback retain
their existing path. Independent producer CPU/children, complete eligibility,
accepted durable effects and completion reservations before PREPARE, and
required-mode activation remain unfinished. No provider fanout or PDF prefetch
is enabled by this change. The full design remains incomplete.

## Borrowed execution IO in owner operations (2026-10-20)

Source `634626b904c19a1cc190ce0a7691b0ca99de2628`: controlled writes now borrow the request executor, or the configured host
executor when the request has none. They no longer construct a per-request
thread pool. Deadline clocks remain separate from execution IO. Native
BEGIN/PREPARE/resolve/ACK, status reads and configured owner waits preserve this
selection; malformed explicit descriptors fail without choosing another pool.
Production owner sources already attach the host BackendRuntime. Unconfigured
legacy maintenance and acquisition waits retain their standalone fallback.

PreDecisionContext carries the borrowed executor through compiled callbacks.
Its fromRequest helper preserves lifetime and IO without lending coordinator
CPU to participant children. OwnerTransition.wait uses its original execution
IO while retiring capture and lending CPU before retry. Native ABI 49 fences
the private layout change; shared status numbers and durable formats do not
change.

This corrects an earlier source-level gap: fc34f7465f supplied the provider IO
descriptor from a newly created executor. Its direct DB fixture proved that a
supplied descriptor survived preparation, but did not prove caller-executor
reuse through the source controller.

regressions. Three IO-selection cases have unchanged-source passing evidence;
they cover caller precedence, configured fallback, missing/malformed authority
and caller capacity refusal. The unchanged public consumer passes 25/25
ReleaseSafe build steps against the immutable source commit. These are module
composition checks, without linked provider products. `caller-executor-verified.json`
binds the exact source hashes and records qualification limits.
Source-controller and range-dispatch checks remain semantic;
the small linked visibility fixture proves its contract only. Full linked
storage archive/cold-source runtime remain unqualified; full Linux
qualification is waived.

Independent producer CPU and children outside retained holders, durable accepted

## Original authority through provider control boundaries (2026-10-20)

Source `aec0358112df715a12fac03bd0184a82df57a60d` preserves fallible request authority through
inference checks and the production asset runtime's composed cancellation. Each
invocation remembers its first rejection atomically, so a boolean transport poll
cannot consume a one-shot error and let later work resume. Composition advertises
a fallible check only when an underlying authority supplies one; atomic-only
transport cancellation retains its compatibility behavior. No request control is
installed on the shared lifecycle runtime.

Dense/sparse wrappers recheck authority after input sanitization and before
provider dispatch. Contextual parts/raster callbacks can run without an unused
legacy callback. Asset calls with a finite deadline, borrowed execution or
fallible authority reject unscoped generation and memory planning. Value-scoped
asset calls also enforce the rule for scalar, batched, reported and raster work,
capability queries and batch planning. Controlled scalar fallback remains valid;
an uncontrolled batch callback cannot hide it. Late rejection frees owned output
before acceptance, including partial batches. Quota translation applies only to
actual OutOfMemory, preserving a different original failure after an allocation
denial. Asset request-context helpers retain the inference cancellation/timeout aliases.

Native ABI 47 fences the changed private control layouts. API ABI 55,
storage-owner ABI 109, runnable ABI 16, runtime-failure ABI 66, engine descriptor
29 and reader floor 10 remain unchanged; there is no durable format change.

`provider-original-controls-v7` passes 88/88 build steps: 36 provider-control
cases, 21 PDF/funding cases and a 42-case inference test binary containing two
native HTTP deadline contracts, a discovery sentinel and companions. The focused cases verify
original rejection during sanitization without dispatch, contextual-only raster
support, strict callback/planning selection, controlled fallback, late output
retirement, first-error retention after a transport poll and quota-error identity.
The immutable-context fixture now uses a valid deadline; a separate expired call
must fail before provider work. Both startup profiles and the source controller
have semantic analysis only; full linked archive/cold-source runtime remain
unqualified.

Final qualification source `a5f1fdeb2d6ad8321c852c3a66dce8b9f74724ed` also includes the pinned
generated error-name table and two passing name round-trip cases. The table adds
three test names; shared numeric status identities remain unchanged.

`provider-original-controls-verified.json` binds 5260 unchanged native inputs,
4544 matching immutable public sources, generated-name/source-boundary checks
and all 25 passing ReleaseSafe consumer steps.

At this checkpoint, generated-effect preparation still needed its per-request

## Caller-funded precommit producer planning (2026-10-20)

Source `7ca0f1d0b40aa424d5de9ca8ebfe8881772706cb` connects generated-document preparation to
the caller's preparation allocator. Invocation storage, ownership state, consumer
configuration/plans, masks and coordinator-owned job metadata retain that allocator
until the invocation's physical children join and teardown completes. Each shared
PDF scheduler stores its allocator explicitly; nested runtime activity cannot
change allocation/free ownership. The shared lifecycle runtime and provider state
remain borrowed.

Native page buffers, replay segments, optional result staging and independently
admitted inference outputs keep their existing physical grants and raw backing.
Charging those allocations through the preparation allocator again would count
physical memory twice. Asynchronous workers retain their independently admitted
allocation views; they do not borrow the coordinator's allocator.

Native ABI 46 rejects older private execution layouts. API ABI 55, storage-owner
ABI 109, runnable ABI 16, runtime-failure ABI 66, engine descriptor 29 and reader
floor 10 remain unchanged. No new durable transaction format is introduced.

use after that failure, and complete metadata release after joined work. Existing
native window/grant, cache reclamation and document artifact reuse checks pass.
The aggregate-pressure fixture provisions identity metadata explicitly while
retaining its 64 KiB payload ceiling and original pressure thresholds. Both startup

archive/cold-source runtime remain unqualified.

## Scoped resource stages through borrowed executions (2026-10-20)

Source `4e43317f563766329da969438208fbba16ae1571` adds the following capability.
Borrowed original executions now expose a synchronous, checked resource stage.

with CPU, and detaches the temporary participant before every return. The native
bridge preserves arbitrary original restriction failures and remembers their
cause for later lifetime/checkpoint calls. No new operation, deadline or resource
ledger is created. Physical bundle credit remains owned until all allocations

restriction is checked again after policy validation can perform IO. Missing
capabilities and malformed frames fail before parking. Retained completion and
control roots still reject incremental bundles; this does not authorize fresh
post-decision resource demand. A failed attachment stops the retained waiter.

10 and durable transaction formats remain unchanged.

## Independently prepared online status owners (2026-10-20)

Source `090dc709dce3b77143bc5444f9013c7e1fd13625` schedules current online owner
preparation after a genuine ordinary typed-status residency miss. The miss still
returns availability failure, never successful absence. A caller-side rejection
trace prevents original admission failures from becoming preparation requests.
Hidden restore status does not enqueue public-catalog work.

The queue owns at most 64 fixed-size group/table requests, including active
work. It copies at most 255 name bytes, performs no allocation and retains no
foreground execution, I/O or descriptor. Coalescing, retries and workspace
growth preserve each accepted request's original 30-second native expiry.
Expired requests drop. Preparation uses the existing independently reserved
opening worker and background admission; release/close progress stays on the
other worker. Committed cold opens take priority. New apply debt preempts an
online admission or initial quorum wait so certification cannot wait on an
opening request behind itself. Once certification crosses that dependency,
physical opening finishes without apply-driven cancellation. Shutdown still
cancels the entire attempt. Optional preparation never retires a busy historical
apply owner.

Each attempt funds its workspace before allocating it. The workspace starts at
64 KiB and grows on capture exhaustion through a new admitted attempt, without
renewing expiry. Scheduler/process limits remain authoritative. Descriptor
capture and confirmation use checked caller-owned memory. The producer obtains
quorum authority, captures fresh metadata, opens a current owner, captures again
and compares generation, identity, schema, indexes, restore binding and initial
range with cooperative 4096-byte string checks. Retained quorum, root generation
and publication checks precede readiness. A new owner remains marked pending
until confirmation; status cannot borrow it early. A public preparation cannot
retire or inherit a racing private restore owner. Historical owners remain
ineligible for required status until a current owner is actually prepared.

The producer uses checked read-execution suspension during quorum/metadata I/O.
CPU can be borrowed by foreground work and resumes only after original lifetime
checks. The public read budget now exposes lifetime-only checks with sticky
original errors, so a registry scan never parks or reacquires CPU while locked.
The original deadline, shutdown cancellation and all physical ownership survive
through join. This does not establish interruptibility of every native-open I/O.

actual source scheduling/pending/confirmation/lifetime/suspension/preemption
runtime checks, queue and scheduler tests, the persistent metadata C bridge,
transaction and fanout runtime suites, and controller/status plus both
production startup-profile analysis checks. The final focused build passes
108/108 steps and 14/14 standard tests. Native cold-open completion through
readiness and private-restore/busy-historical admission guards are analyzed
rather than full linked runtime qualified. The immutable public package has 4483

descriptor 28, API kernel 53, file floor 7 and Raft protocol 25 remain

The broader text-statistics controls suite is still failing. A one-file baseline

## Funded cold Raft owner opening (2026-10-20)

Source `e83e2d9a1b090aac7ad0f597cdba30b6a1968746` gives cold committed-Raft
owner opening an independently admitted background execution. The existing
bounded request queue retains its exact committed descriptors and durable retry
behavior. Each attempt has its own 30-second native deadline, including
scheduler waiting, shutdown cancellation and checked retained descriptor memory.
It waits on ordinary background capacity instead of spending protected health or
cleanup capacity.

A separately reserved worker drains atomic lease releases and retired-owner
close debt while the opening worker waits for admission. The data runtime
reserves two bounded node workers for this source, rather than adding any worker
per connection or per group. Failed partial startup signals and joins the first
task before returning; shutdown wakes and joins both tasks before the hosting
worker and scheduler leases are released. Retrying opens never abandons physical
work when its logical attempt expires.

Native cancellation predicates check lifetime without parking or reacquiring CPU
under a storage lock. Admission is checked before registry access and cold
opening. A physically completed open is registered even if its attempt expired
during native I/O, so durable replay can reuse it on retry instead of repeatedly
closing and reopening the same database. The expired attempt still returns its
original rejection and retains execution through physical return. This is not a
claim that every native-open I/O operation is interruptible.

and routing-bridge checks plus analysis of the actual cold-open controller,

qualified. The new public package has 4483 matching sources and passes 25

43, owner ABI 103, engine descriptor 28, API kernel 53, file floor 7 and Raft
protocol 25 remain unchanged. Full Linux qualification remains waived.

## Typed owner and RPC status delivery (2026-10-19)

Source `d56003bd208e325e09d0c81e1370ec50efd46389` distinguishes an absent
transaction record from a failed status read. Required status never treats an error named
`TxnNotFound` as absence or permission to begin. Known decisions retain actual
saved status, mode and binding. Both coordinator abort confirmations and
ambiguous commit recovery preserve that distinction.

The additive storage-owner C operation resets its result before validation and
reads the actual retained native record under the existing shared apply fence.
It distinguishes a missing record from every original read rejection. Because
the C status enum cannot enumerate arbitrary original controls, the Zig client
retains a caller-side rejection trace before translating status. Native ABI is
43 and storage-owner ABI is 102; engine descriptor 28, API kernel 53, file floor
7 and Raft protocol 25 remain unchanged.

The private existing transaction-status route accepts a fixed 112-byte ATPS
query and returns a fixed 200-byte ATPR reply. Both are versioned and
checksummed. The reply correlates transaction ID, group, hidden scope and plan
before saved binding validation. The client bounds response buffering,
authenticates with the existing service principal and forwards the bounded
server status budget with its client response reserve. Old JSON status remains
available to legacy callers; required workers refuse legacy, stripped or
mismatched replies.

The owner source requires original deadline/admission and borrows existing node
or request I/O. It borrows an already resident owner of the exact physical
identity/generation, validates hidden bootstrap scope/plan and certifies quorum
before the snapshot, then revalidates retained authority and physical generation
afterward. Acquisition fails immediately on registry contention or a required
open/transition. Atomic deferred release cannot join a concurrent cold open or
create a temporary executor. The independent release worker must already be
running. Cold owners must be prepared by an independent funded control path.
Public descriptor capture carries original read admission.

Production metadata routing currently ignores its budget argument. A new
capability for bounded capture defaults false, and the hosted required-status worker
refuses that path until a provider qualifies capture, allocation, traversal and
waiting under the original budget/admission. The local worker and the private
RPC delivery primitives are wired. No required mutation capability is enabled.

the owner-adapter analysis check (six runtime targets passed; owner analysis:
54/54 steps succeeded). Selected runtime cases cover explicit absence, all wire
identity fields, corrupt/truncated and legacy replies, original failures at
every codec checkpoint, authenticated RPC, local dispatch and unavailable
routing. The persistent bound-Raft test exercises the actual production C entry
in both modes on pending and committed records before/after reopen, and
validates original caller rejection traces at every checkpoint. Owner residency,
nonblocking release and unbounded-quorum refusal regressions are analyzed
without the full storage archive; their full linked runtime suite remains
unqualified. The immutable public package has 4,483 exact exported sources and
passes 25 ReleaseSafe consumer steps. Runtime inputs are hashed. The final
owner-only readiness gate and fixture correction pass a separate analysis check;
all other runtime source inputs match committed source. Both receipts record the

## Binding-aware coordinator status (2026-10-19)

Commit `141e2a2f824c518a7081444fd0e55fe6ce402c08` adds typed status evidence
carrying the actual durable status, original preparation mode and
participant/route binding. The coordinator compares that evidence with its
retained original cohort for pending/terminal retries and ambiguous commit
recovery. Missing mode or binding cannot qualify a committed required
transaction. Every group, epoch, participant or route mismatch prevents follower
commit propagation; required status never falls back to a mode-only legacy read. Expected
binding values are comparisons, not evidence returned by a provider.

Final source `85e2ca05fac9ced3552bf1960ad40cb702f325b0` also verifies both
abort-confirmation paths: the BEGIN contact-mask path and the later full-cohort
path. A mismatched bound abort cannot authorize follower cleanup. Legacy aborts
remain terminal after their sidecars retire. Required abort observations have a
finite recovery deadline bounded by completion authority; ordinary legacy status
behavior is preserved.

The native DB read `getTransactionPreparationDecision` captures status, mode and
binding under one shared apply fence. It yields through original read admission
while a writer holds that fence, preserves original errors (including
errors that resemble missing keys), and releases its lock on every rejection. It reads
retained history after accepted effect frames retire, and performs no producer
work or query/index admission. Its caller must establish the appropriate
quorum/owner read barrier and hidden-owner authorization before reading local
storage. This local snapshot alone does not establish distributed authority or
readiness.

The new `bound_retained_contract` capability defaults false and is required
before fresh required BEGIN. Native ABI is 42 and engine descriptor 28; storage
owner ABI 101, file floor 7 and Raft protocol 25 are unchanged. The shared error
registry now includes `PreparationRequirementMismatch`.

`native-bound-status-v3-verified.json` records six focused native targets (Build
Summary: 108/108 steps succeeded; 16/16 tests passed) and 184 selected cases.
Four new coordinator regressions cover all binding-field drift, hidden
scope/plan drift, ambiguous commit replies, both abort replies, terminal legacy
aborts and refusal of legacy status fallback in both modes. The persistent
bound-Raft test also exercises the actual native snapshot before/after
resolution and reopen, every original error at every read checkpoint, and
original rejections while waiting on a held write fence. Existing SQL/HTTP session, cohort,
ownership and control-progress regressions pass.

The immutable public package from `141e2a2f824c518a7081444fd0e55fe6ce402c08`
passes 25 ReleaseSafe consumer steps; all 4,483 exported sources match final

first durable cohort. Failed persistence cannot contact a participant; retries

## Durable participant and route bindings (2026-10-19)

Commit `2d3896d6313deb5e59701d6b24b90a83e6044960` persists the exact group,

seal and terminal history. Earlier unbound records stay readable but cannot gain
binding authority through an idempotent retry or qualify a bound receipt. Legacy
prepare/seal entry points cannot drop an existing binding.

The distinct `begin_bound_v1`, `prepare_bound_v1` and `seal_bound_v1` commands carry
the binding in canonical fixed-width hex. Apply validates the group, epoch and
scoped participant identity, then preserves the exact BEGIN binding through intent
publication and atomic sealing. Changed route or participant bindings cannot
advance the ordered receipt. Receipt fields are reconstructed from the durable
binding and fully inspected accepted frame; caller-supplied expected fields only
validate the result. Terminal resolution retires effects while retaining mode and
binding under the existing history/expiry rules.

Reader floor/catalog envelope 7 protect v8 records, including after sidecars
retire. Native ABI is 40, engine descriptor 27 and bound commands require Raft
protocol 25; storage owner ABI remains 101. Older active preparation metadata
still requires resolution or coordinated migration before enabling the new floor.
These hashes preserve a route agreement; the route owner must establish fresh
authority before BEGIN. Apply performs no metadata RPC and does not infer route
authority from a digest alone.

## Replicated required PREPARE and final seal (2026-10-19)

Commit `629a03a2594ff9a6329a7452c77a350d111aee80` adds distinct
`prepare_required_v1` and `seal_required_v1` internal commands. Required PREPARE
checks the durable BEGIN mode before preparation and again under apply before
publishing intents and its ordered receipt. Replicated transforms must already
be expanded. A final seal carries immutable precomputed effect bytes; apply
validates their transaction, intent revision/digest, schema, catalog and mode,
then commits the accepted frame, backlog accounting and ordered receipt together.
It invokes no producer. Different output cannot replace the first accepted frame.
Identical retries preserve its grant while advancing a new receipt.

Already-applied PREPARE and seal entries return from their durable receipts before
fresh admission or attempts to rewrite frozen intents. Seals survive reopen and
are consumed by ordinary resolution even when its acknowledgement level is
weaker than the original mode. Effect sidecars retire while the agreed mode stays
in the existing terminal record. Stale frames and mode conflicts cannot advance
ordered progress. Nonreplicated required commands refuse the legacy fallback.

A final seal permits only its transaction, staging scope, timestamp and
acknowledgement fields. Other batch controls fail closed in encoding, decoding
and apply, including newly added controls with nondefault values. Decoded frame
ownership is explicit and released on every parse/allocation failure. The inline
base64 command is bounded by the existing 64 MiB request envelope; the durable
codec's full 64 MiB frame limit still needs a large-payload transport path.

Native ABI is 39 and engine descriptor 26; storage owner ABI remains 101 and
permanent file floor remains 6. PREPARE/seal select Raft protocol 24. The existing
proposal gate also covers both commands, before any barrier or entry. Decoder
support is not coordinated migration or real producer/provider readiness.

## Finite public HTTP processing and physical output (2026-10-16)

Canonical `admission.max_request_duration_ms` now defaults to 300,000 ms and
accepts 1 ms through one day. Public transport configuration applies that ceiling
and preserves an explicitly tighter transport limit. Generic httpx embeddings
can still choose their own policy. H1 captures one deadline before request-body
buffering and keeps it across lazy input, dispatch, response delivery and drain;
keep-alive idle time is separate. H2 stores a stream-local deadline before handler
publication, and buffered plus streaming writes use the same controlled header,
flow-credit and socket-write paths. An intrinsic copied deadline composes with
application cancellation and CPU-wait callbacks without retaining a moved local
wrapper. A body-budget calculation now propagates expiry instead of falling back
to an older reader deadline.

Testing also exposed a pre-existing Darwin receive failure after complete
half-closed responses: changing SO_RCVTIMEO can fail after both FINs complete.
The receive path now recognizes readable EOF with a nonblocking, non-consuming
peek in that specific option-error case. Reset, invalid-descriptor and live-socket
option errors retain their failure behavior. Existing FIN, pipeline and hard-reset
cases pass; FIN cases run both without a transport ceiling and with a five-second
ceiling.

The preceding HTTP-lifetime run passes all 80 build steps. The full HTTP suite has
687 passes and 14 skips; the H2-flow suite has 33 passes and three skips. Nine named
transport cases, nine API deadline/configuration cases, one common-config case
and the startup envelope case also pass. These selections overlap; they are not
independent counts of unique contracts. Source/schema/cache guards and an
independent current-input hash check pass. Receipt: `http-request-lifetime-verified`.

Initial filtered HTTP and isolated FIN runs accidentally selected no tests because
the umbrella import-discovery test did not match their filters. They are explicitly
excluded from HTTP qualification in `http-request-lifetime-verification-corrections`.
A dedicated matching discovery root, strict runner and named inventory now prevent
that false green. The initial full-suite TLS failure used system Python without
TLS 1.3; the final run uses the installed supported Python/OpenSSL runtime.

H2 framing now captures its budget when the first frame bytes arrive, retains it
through CONTINUATION reassembly, and carries the original request timestamp into
the stream before HPACK decoding. A timeout after consuming partial framing is
terminal for the connection; the frame pump shuts down physical I/O before joined
teardown. Idle receive timeouts with no consumed bytes remain retryable. Completed
streams retain their independent flow-credit and output deadlines.

The focused physical run passes twelve named cases, including six real TCP stall
scenarios spanning partial frame headers, partial HEADERS payloads and missing
CONTINUATION frames, with either the header or request ceiling tighter. Scripted
clock tests also verify nonrenewal and preservation through decode. Receipt:
`h2-ingress-deadline-physical-v2`. Its preceding sandboxed run failed socket setup;
it supplies no product-failure evidence. The subsequent current-source broader
run passes all 80 build steps: 691 HTTP cases with 14 skips, 33 H2-flow cases with
three skips, all 13 named transport cases including idle-timeout recovery, nine
API deadline/configuration cases, the common-config case and startup envelope.
These selections overlap. Independent source/schema/log hashes and the complete
named transport inventory match. Receipt: `h2-ingress-deadline-verified.json`.

This is not the completed whole-HTTP lifetime policy. Tighter application
budgets must be enforced through opaque lazy-body and stream callbacks rather than
relying only on the host transport ceiling. Actual separately compiled API/runtime
integration after API ABI 47 also remains pending. Accepted durable work continues
to use its independent completion/recovery ownership; these checks do not qualify
all write paths, other frontends, resource profiles or production borrowing.

## Synchronous opaque HTTP controls (2026-10-16)

The shared HTTP ABI now offers controlled lazy-body reads and controlled stream
start, write and close callbacks. Each receives a synchronous, borrowed check and
remaining-time view. The host intersects it with its own request control during
physical I/O; monitors can poll those checks without changing CPU ownership.
Returned writers keep only the host's original control. Each later operation
installs its own borrowed view and restores the original before returning,
including failed I/O. Body readers likewise restore their scoped controls.
Installed host execution-wait hooks remain separate and now also cover body I/O.

Native receives poll the same read after byte-free timeout results; they do not
race multiple consumers. The std.Io receive monitor joins its operation before

## Native-clock inference and controlled worker events (2026-10-16)

An explicit native-clock callback now lets httpx project an application deadline
into transport controls without rewriting the timestamp consumed by native
execution. The projection samples the target clock first. Unknown native
timestamps still acquire no implicit clock authority. Inference installs its
actual monotonic clock; worker events carry a conservative scalar deadline,
never callback pointers. Millisecond rounding tightens the projected ceiling by
at most one millisecond instead of granting extra time.

Controlled child start/write/close callbacks wait for the parent's acknowledgment.
If the child's control expires while the parent sink is blocked, a sequenced
cancellation frame bypasses ordinary payload admission. The parent's scoped
event control observes that frame during physical I/O. The child remains stopped
until the sink returns and acknowledgment arrives, or the endpoint is fenced.
Pending sequence checks prevent an old event's cancellation from affecting a
later event or request. The internal framing magic is AFW6 and worker wire version
is 13; C ABI versions remain API 48, inference-host 38 and local-inference 4.

Parent output combines the original native deadline, event deadline and event
cancellation. Check callbacks remain monitor-safe and never checkpoint a CPU
grant. CPU transitions stay on the caller's existing execution-wait interface,
which is installed before lazy-body reads and cleared after joined dispatch.
An unsupported streaming-body handoff refuses before blocking. Local recorded
reentry errors retain their identity through the C callback result. Endpoint
closure now rejects resumption before a lost acknowledgment, leaving the loan
parked for the existing fence and cleanup owner.

All 104 scoped build steps pass. Named evidence includes 27 RPC cases, two control
adapter cases, five inference-parent phase cases including the production child
callbacks and parent decoder over real pipes, six wire cases, the actual subprocess
backpressure fixture, and fifteen lifetime plus fifteen opaque-adapter cases.
The full HTTP suite passes 693 cases with fourteen skips. Selections overlap and
can reuse valid cached results. Real pipe/H2 checks verify a child cancellation
interrupts blocked DATA credit, keeps the child stopped until acknowledgment,
clears borrowed controls and leaves a subsequent RPC healthy. The dedicated
cancellation/timeout schedule saturates payload counters; it does not establish
an operating-system memory-pressure envelope. Receipt:
`worker-http-control-verified.json`.

policy. This matches the existing internal-admin default and also covers public,
inference and standby clients that use the common owned client.

## Bound standby discovery metadata and keep admission lightweight (2026-10-16)

A real HTTP deadline regression showed a mutation discovery request returning
the first 404 after its body read had exceeded the original deadline. The read
negotiator now checks that original context immediately after inspecting the
body and before fallback. Cancellation is preserved and no mutation is sent.
Unavailable/unauthorized discovery responses also no longer publish a successful
route choice.

The process-wide route accelerator now keeps at most 256 targets with copied
keys of at most 4 KiB each. A fixed ring evicts old accelerator entries; live
clients keep their own pinned route. Larger URLs skip the global cache.
Updates use fixed slots so replacing a cached value cannot retain the caller's
larger string backing allocation. Reset drops all retained key references.
Focused tests cover eviction, updates, oversized keys, reset and concurrent
lookup/publication under the race detector. This bounds copied keys and entry
count; it is not a whole-process resident-memory qualification.

Admission now lives in a standard-library-only SDK subpackage. Public SDK
names are aliases and constructors delegate to that same owner; admin clients
use the small package without importing public query/schema dependencies.
The need was verified by an operator setup failure from the earlier top-level
SDK dependency. No operator dependency files were changed to hide that coupling.
The common owner also exposes a coherent capacity/policy snapshot, used by the
existing cancellation/FIFO/reentrant-context tests.

## Reserved policy-validation memory before experimental CPU work (2026-10-16)

The SQL adapter can now preclaim a fixed foreground buffer before enabling a
captured-table CPU stage. The buffer comes from the node request-memory owner;
it is held alongside prepared numeric scratch across CPU return and queue waits.
A validation borrows a fixed-buffer allocator only until its nested catalog,
schema and credential arenas retire. It cannot fall back to the general heap or
consume protected control memory. The buffer is returned at read-fence retirement
without requiring another CPU grant. Zero, over-one-MiB and unavailable
reservations refuse before publication.

Preflight validates current captured authority using that same buffer, then
checks the original execution lifetime after catalog IO. Independent SQL-context
clocks cannot publish a reservation after its owning deadline, cancellation or
scheduler closure. Captured-table loan eligibility requires this reservation.
This is a bound on accepted storage, not a promise that arbitrary future policy
shapes fit: later growth can return OutOfMemory before output. Empty-table stages
retain their existing no-catalog behavior.

Reserved validation derives schema in caller storage even when the optional
schema cache is warm. This accounts for uncached derivation during preflight and
avoids depending on a later cache slot or backing allocation. Ordinary schema
resolution also treats busy builder slots as an uncached fallback. The focused
cache fixture models four occupied builder slots; it does not run four independent
builder actors.

The native captured-stage fixture fills foreground capacity with both prepared
scratch and a 64-KiB policy buffer. Unreserved validation demonstrably fails at
that pressure while reserved validation succeeds. A real live principal, schema,
binding and row-policy generation survive unchanged CPU handoff; changed catalog,
policy generation and credentials reject before output. The growth schedule
expands the live row filter beyond the reservation during CPU return: validation
refuses, caches no authority, retires its arena, keeps the original root and
memory charges, and leaves control allocation available. Restoring the smaller
policy permits another validation using the same buffer; the failed operation's
numeric output is never exposed.

experimental captured stage. Complete profile bounds, measured stage time and
actual compiled API integration remain open before production operator lending.
Full qualification remains waived.

## Preserve validated live grants while lending excess CPU (2026-10-16)

A prepared stage can now move its already-running CPU grant onto eligible
above-floor reserve when ordinary work is queued. The same root remains running:
its resume generation, quantum, checkpoint count, deadline and charges do not
change. General work is dispatched through the existing weighted queues. If the
released general capacity cannot fit the queued team, the loan converts back
immediately; team assembly and the hard floor remain intact. The default
single-slot bounded reserve still permits no lending. Parking clears eligibility
and returns CPU through the original retained owner.

This avoids suspending a just-validated stage solely to obtain a loan. Its
copied-input arithmetic can run on the same validated grant; returning the loan
then reacquires ordinary CPU and validates current policy before output. It does
not allow a suspended/resumed root to bypass policy validation or authorize IO
inside a prepared stage.

The new native SQL fixture uses a real captured table binding, schema cache,
active row-policy generation, live authenticated principal and row filter. A
64-row prepared addition runs on the transferred live grant without provider
reads or catalog calls; bounded floor work and a queued write-class entry also
hold their grants. After CPU return, the unchanged case validates successfully
and exposes exact 42 results. Catalog generation change, row-policy generation
change and credential revocation during the return wait each reject before the
private result is exposed. Original deadline, 23 retained bytes and ingress
ownership survive the handoff. The scratch allocation fills its finite foreground
allowance and returns that entire charge on retirement; control allocation is
independent.

Scope limit: this fixture's catalog allocations use a separate testing allocator,
not the saturated numeric scratch partition. It proves the captured-policy/CPU
state transition, not complete request-heap progress or a reserved minimum policy
working set. Establish that resource bundle and measured interval bounds before
production lending. No production operator enables borrowing yet.

The live-transfer regression fails before the core change. All 102 core tests now
pass, including default-floor preservation and refusal to retain an unusable loan
while a queued team assembles. `live-validated-cpu-stage-native-v2` passes all 74
build steps and seven custom API cases; the 22-case numeric suite is reused from
v1 with unchanged numeric/core inputs. V1's owned-principal fixture type error is
retained, not treated as qualification. Independent
`live-validated-cpu-stage-verified.json` records this scope and source/schema/cache
preservation. Actual compiled API/pgwire integration and full design qualification
remain open.

## Prepared numeric instruction continuations (2026-10-16)

Prepared coordinator math now retains an explicit next-instruction cursor in
its existing fixed scratch owner. Each `step()` executes one instruction over
at most 64 rows, including any integer-width validation, or the final root
output pass. That bounds a call to 128 instruction/cell-and-width steps (64 root
visits for output), with at most 65 calls per 64-instruction chunk. The overall
8256-cell-step limit is unchanged. No provider, allocator, coercion, IO or
scheduling callback runs inside a math step. `run()` remains a convenience drain
of these same steps and does not qualify a whole chunk for borrowing.

The SQL coordinator checkpoints before every step and before copying completed
output. Intermediate values and the cursor stay private in the charged scratch
while it waits for the original CPU grant; no child execution, replacement root
or deadline is created. Cancellation, expiry or revoked policy discards that
continuation before result publication. Width/arithmetic failures invalidate it;
repreparation resets the cursor and cannot expose an old result.

Two cadence regressions fail before integration. The passing native suite proves
all 64 instruction boundaries with changed provider storage and all further
allocations refused, exact narrow-integer results, failure/reprepare isolation,
and a queued write-class scheduler entry plus protected control progressing before chunk
publication on one shared ordinary CPU. The existing scalar/vector, native-regex
mutation-cancellation and all eighteen ordered-stream schedules also pass.
The finite foreground scratch-owner case and five scalar/SQL-policy boundary
cases pass, with API owner analysis. `prepared-numeric-step-after-native-v1`
succeeds at all 74 build steps: 22 stock-runner cases and six custom API cases.
Named binary rerun and independent `prepared-numeric-step-verified.json` confirm
coverage and unchanged source, schema and cache inputs.

This is a smaller cooperative work interval in the production coordinator path,
not a measured maximum elapsed time, a private-heap graph proof or enabled CPU
lending. Time/resource qualification, successful captured-policy validation
around an actual borrowed operator and compiled API/pgwire integration remain
open. The full design and its other operator/frontend families remain in scope.

## SQL provider stage return before catalog validation (2026-10-16)

SQL's custom provider now exposes the existing checked CPU-stage capability.
Enabling requires an active SQL context and a read guard, validates the current
fence, and delegates budget and lifetime checks to the original execution.
Disabling returns CPU first, then checks the SQL context and fence. An independently
expired SQL context therefore cannot leave stage eligibility active. Malformed
ABI prefixes and enable flags refuse without changing the owner or eligibility.
This callback is trusted internal capability plumbing; no production SQL operator
calls it yet and no frontend plan gains bounded eligibility.

`validateReadPins` now ends an eligible stage before its first allocation or
catalog call. This happens only when the guard invokes actual validation. Cached
checks and scalar lifetime polls do not allocate, wait or refresh ordinary CPU
quanta. Guard validation retains its existing conservative generation cache:
returning CPU may cause the next check to validate again. It does not treat a
pre-wait grant as a new lifetime or a broader policy authority.

The new native coordinator regression fails before the change because catalog
validation reaches a live CPU loan. Four passing schedules now prove no catalog
calls while queued for ordinary CPU, bounded-floor progress, and original

Production stage time/resources, successful captured-policy validation around a

The shared per-worker validation hook now ends a prepared CPU-loan stage before

without lending eligibility leave their quantum, checkpoint count and resume

## Original hard-floor requirement for CPU lending (2026-10-16)

The original design requires a nonborrowable floor at every stage and borrowing
only above those floors. The former experimental one-slot reserve lent the
entire protected slot; earlier cooperative-return receipts do not prove a hard
floor. The scheduler now makes the default one-slot reserve nonborrowable and
supports explicit `bounded_read_slots` above one as elastic capacity inside the
same total slot ceiling. One bounded CPU always stays unavailable to borrowers;
at most one excess CPU may be lent. General, health and cleanup partitions retain
their own capacity, and CPU loans grant no heap or durable authority.

Focused native core tests pass for the default floor, reserve sizes two through
four with different bounded occupancy, immediate floor admission without a
borrower checkpoint, reclaim, cancellation, expiry, close and cleanup. Explicit
reserve validation and quota-constrained automatic fallback are covered. New
Prometheus floor and loan-capacity gauges derive from the same captured reserve;
extern telemetry and runnable capability layouts do not change. This proves
scheduler CPU ownership, not dedicated OS cores or full operator qualification.

The shared local-worker validation hook now regains ordinary CPU before full
policy validation. SQL's separate custom provider path now has the checked boundary as well;
production operator time/resource proof remains open. No production operator
opts into lending.
Earlier receipts predate both this correction and the latest main merge; their
coverage is historical. Full qualification remains waived.

## Prepared numeric coordinator integration (2026-10-16)

Short scoped numeric vector evaluation now prepares and runs fixed 64-row chunks
on its existing execution. Scratch is allocated once through the scope's finite
node foreground allocator, reused across chunks, and freed before returning.
Chunk output is copied to the caller only after the owner checkpoint succeeds.
Checks precede preparation, each resumable arithmetic instruction and publication; cancellation, expiry or
policy failure discards the result and releases scratch without retiring the
ingress owner. Missing optional scratch preserves the existing serial fallback.
Typed bulk column fill avoids repeated per-cell column lookup.

A distinct `CoordinatorScope` carries the original execution, allocator and
checkpoint hook, without worker IO, wait boundary or submission methods. Parallel
`ExecutionScope` remains separate. SQL adapters publish coordinator scope for
scheduled reads even when pgwire requires serial execution; parallel scope
remains disabled there. The API hook uses its existing context/read-fence
checkpoint after scheduler reentry. Read-stream, aggregate and relational call
sites carry both views, and the relational wrapper retains the original owner.
Single-program serial and dictionary cohorts use the prepared path; unsupported
and multi-program fused cases retain ordinary execution. No fresh root, deadline
or CPU-loan authority is constructed.

`prepared-numeric-coordinator-native-v7` passes 65 build steps, eighteen native
cases and one API-owner case, plus API owner-boundary analysis. Six numeric
component cases, three coordinator cases and three existing vector regressions
pass; the remaining cases include the ordered SQL stream fixture and five module
anchors. That stream fixture runs nine schedules with and without parallel
scope: exact ordered 10,000-row results, filters, LIMIT/OFFSET, arithmetic failure
continuation, early close, cancellation, expiry, policy revocation and registry
pressure. Coordinator-only execution makes no cursor splits or child submissions.
The API-owner test fills the exact foreground scratch envelope (including its
allocation header), refuses an extra foreground allocation, preserves control
allocation and releases the entire charge. Earlier fixture syntax/import/type
failures remain recorded. `prepared-numeric-coordinator-verified.json` verifies
current source/schema/log/binary hashes, every named case and the eighteen stream
schedules. This is native pipeline/source-wiring evidence; the actual compiled
API protocol run remains pending after the earlier cache loss.

CPU borrowing and production bounded classification remain disabled for these
operators. Next work must qualify non-yielding execution time and the complete
scratch/continuation/worker graph, bind an explicit prepared CPU phase on the
original owner, return any loan before preparation or fallback, and verify its
checked callbacks and protected arrivals through the actual compiled API.

## Prepared numeric fixed scratch (2026-10-16)

`sql/typed_kernel.zig` now exposes `PreparedNumeric`, a single-program scratch
owner limited to 64 instructions and 64 rows. Initialization checks supported
numeric/boolean/null operations and operand order before publishing the owner.
Strings, lazy operators, exact-decimal and float4 paths retain their existing
fallback. The owner allocates fixed scratch once; `scratch_bytes` reports its
struct footprint, with allocator overhead still belonging to the caller's heap.
The caller must retain its allocator and immutable bound program through this
owner's lifetime, and retire every borrowed result before the next preparation
or destruction.

Preparation performs provider reads and parameter coercion outside the arithmetic
interval and copies the resulting numeric values. A failed preparation exposes
no new chunk. The arithmetic pass reads only copied instructions, numeric scratch
and copied root metadata; it invokes no allocator/provider/wait callback. It
visits at most 4096 instruction cells, 4096 width-check cells and 64 root cells.
These 8256 cell steps are an algorithmic bound, not a measured time bound.
Errors invalidate the chunk without publishing partially computed results.

`prepared-numeric-fixed-scratch-native-v2` passes five component tests plus three
module anchors. Tests compare exact integer/float/boolean/null behavior and
error identities with scalar execution, reject unsupported preparation without

after preparation, and deny all further scratch allocations during evaluation.
The named binary rerun and source/schema/log/binary hashes are independently

The coordinator integration above now wires this component into ordinary SQL

loans. Time qualification, complete continuation/worker ownership and actual
checked callback/protected-arrival proof remain open. Full bounded-read

## Rust SDK bounded admission (2026-10-16)

The Rust SDK generator now adapts its AST to acquire a shared request permit
before URL/body construction and transfer that permit into the response body.
All 211 generated async methods have both operations; constructors install one
owner and clones share it. Defaults are 100 active, 100 queued and one second of
FIFO waiting. Queue cancellation, expiry and owner close retire their waiters;
selected-but-unpublished work rechecks close. Active bodies retain capacity
through EOF, error or drop, retiring the transport before the permit. Raw error
responses preserve that ownership and original URL/status/headers.

SDK-created reqwest clients have finite per-host idle pools and disable automatic
redirects/retries. Supplied HTTP clients preserve caller policy. The public
admission config/stats/close/share API exposes finite counts and typed unsent
refusals within the generated error envelope. Queue and transport deadlines
remain separate unless the caller wraps the original complete SDK future.
Caller payloads, decoded memory and post-body CPU are not fully bounded by this
HTTP admission owner. WebAssembly qualification remains open.

`rust-sdk-bounded-admission-native-v2` passes 34 tests, including twelve new
admission cases and real TCP proof: an incomplete unread error response holds
capacity across cloned handles, queued/canceled calls send no additional request,
and dropping the response permits a fresh successful request. The final

cases), including mutating SQL against 301/302/303/307/308 responses through

log hashes, all named cases, and all 211 generated operation guards and response
transfers. Earlier baseline and focused runs remain recorded.

## Physical shared SQL worker floor (2026-10-16)

SQL worker factories now expose a fourth shared role, `bounded_read`, with one
physical worker independent of execution, control and cleanup pools. Existing
role selectors keep their values; the new selector is 4 and changes no ABI
layout. Consumers reject malformed bounded-role capacities and retire a failed
borrow without disturbing peers. The final borrower joins callbacks before
returning the node's reservation, including during runtime shutdown.

At the default dedicated-worker ceiling of 32, role capacities are execution 12,
control 5, cleanup 8 and bounded read 1. Acquiring all roles reserves 26 against
the same hard node ceiling. Execution previously provided 11, which was smaller
than the default eight queued requests plus four required progress workers;
`sqlExecutionIo` silently returned general IO in that case. The supported shared
path now publishes the private executor, reserving control and, when isolation is
enabled, the bounded role first. Insufficient explicit queue/worker envelopes
fail before foreground publication. Failed foreground acquisition retains those
protected reservations for a retry and retires them on API shutdown.

`bounded-sql-worker-api-native-v4` passes 69 build steps, eleven stock worker
checks and eight API checks. Tests saturate execution and cleanup while real

thirteen API cases when both cache-root inodes changed and the storage-kernel

## Checked CPU-loan capabilities and telemetry (2026-10-16)

Runnable ABI 14 adds a versioned optional CPU-loan callback to owner and borrowed
execution capabilities. Its options carry only enable/disable and the verified
work bound; no fresh IO, deadline, cancellation, heap or durable authority is
accepted. Prefixes, reserved bytes and option combinations are checked before
callback invocation. Missing capability fails explicitly. `fromOwner` forwards
the optional capability without retaining a new operation.

The API-owned capsule implements the callback through the original execution.
The production local read adapter forwards it with its mandatory validation
hook. Enabling validates current read authority; disabling waits for ordinary
CPU and revalidates after reentry. The native bridge delegates through the
checked C callback and invalidates its local resume generation on a successful
return. A root adapter still cannot retire its ingress owner.

Focused native adapter tests perform an actual CPU loan, disable it while base
CPU is occupied, revoke read policy during that wait, and verify Forbidden on
reentry with a stopped root and retained resources. The successful variant
preserves the same deadline and resumes normally. Missing-capability and
malformed-header tests verify explicit refusal without changing retained root
ownership. These callback fixtures are within one native test binary; they do
not establish a production operator's work bound or a separately compiled
operator's enabled loan path.

Loan active/grant/return fields now join the scheduler's existing locked snapshot
and cross the runtime telemetry layout. Prometheus exports the corresponding
bounded node-level gauge and counters. Active CPU includes each loan once;
operation count and retained memory stay unchanged. API kernel ABI 46 rejects
older contexts before the enlarged embedded telemetry is accessed.

`checked-cpu-borrow-telemetry-native-v2` passes the focused integration and API
analysis (90/90 build steps). It runs 25 owner-port tests and seven canonical
configuration tests freshly, and reuses successful cached results for 96 scheduler,

also pass, including the new coherent metrics check. The initial v1 command
failed only because the new owner fixture requested two CPU slots from a policy
with one general slot. The fixture now has two general slots so the intended

`checked-cpu-borrow-api-layout-native-v1` then rebuilds the actual native archives
and passes all thirteen compiled opaque API cases and three cancellation-mapping

Production operator qualification remains open. Source review finds execution,
