remain pending, so these focused results do not enable defaults.

### Original commit-control callback contract (2026-10-08, focused gates passed)

CommitControl carries the request-owned execution team and original pre-decision
deadline, clock and cancellation independently of post-commit visibility
cancellation. New batch/stable-ID callbacks fail closed when a supplied control
would otherwise be discarded. All six compiled callback tests pass on native
macOS and pinned Nix/glibc Linux, including foreign dispatch and exact fallible
fence errors; [receipts](qualification/workload-pooling/receipts/2026-10-08/sql-commit-control/README.md)
pin the tested RequestContext execution-team field and boundary source. Hosted
worker/retry wiring and its actual no-skip regression are proposed separately
and still require production qualification. Provisioned/bound sources, SQL
ingress adoption and physical durability waits remain pending. Defaults remain
disabled.

Native text scoring now borrows synchronous lifetime authority from the original
storage request. Ordinary and filtered WAND, brute-force scoring, pivot repair,
block interval pruning and competitive block scans check that authority at most
every 64 loop steps. The callback uses the retained runnable owner's clock and
shutdown/cancellation state without acquiring CPU or yielding under index read
locks. A borrowed grant without lifetime support fails closed. Unpooled requests
use their existing monotonic deadline and cancellation token.

`zig build antfly-text-scoring-authority-test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -j1`
checks cancellation, timeout and shutdown during real scoring, partial output
retirement, successful snapshot reuse, unchanged controlled/legacy scores, and
expiration during unscored block pruning. This is focused correctness evidence.
It does not qualify CPU fairness under locks, arbitrary postings decoder work,
phrase/count/sort/aggregation/vector paths, background execution, runtime resource
limits, performance or automatic defaults. Those remain completion requirements.

Both production count-only entry points now retain the same non-suspending
original lifetime authority: exact snapshot counts and materialized candidate
counts. Term postings (including synonym expansion), recursive Boolean clauses,
minimum-should-match accumulation, match-all construction and candidate copying
poll during their loops. Multi-segment offsets and deletion masks retain their
existing semantics. Focused tests compare legacy/controlled membership and
counts, exercise nested Boolean filters across deleted documents, and inject
lifetime failures at every observed checkpoint to check partial retirement.
Specialized leaf filters, bulk bitmap operations, positional verification,
provider/decoder work and lock-safe CPU yielding still need bounded-work coverage;
checks surrounding these operations do not prove bounded execution within them.

Prefix (including companion exact lookup), wildcard, fuzzy, regexp and term-range
filters now pass original lifetime authority into postings scans and request-local
dictionary iterators. Contiguous and range-backed iterators poll while decoding
rejected terms and skipping blocks, including within a single `next()` call that
exposes no accepted entry. Ordinary filter queries, match-all and sorted-query
filter selection retain the authority through the public search dispatcher.
Focused tests compare membership with the legacy paths, reject every observed
checkpoint, and expire no-output iterator scans in both storage representations.
Automaton construction/transitions, bulk bitmap work, specialized leaf filters,
projection/sort/aggregation loops, physical I/O and lock-safe CPU yielding remain
separate bounded-execution requirements. In particular, production text sources
currently retain an analysis read lock for the query's lifetime.

Controlled service-lock acquisition now preserves reader priority and writer
intent while releasing runnable CPU only around the actual timed futex wait.
It polls retained, non-suspending lifetime authority without translating the
owner's deadline into the lock's Io clock. Resume is mandatory before consuming
a wake or reporting an Io error. Failure unwinds registered waiters, writer gate
and intent, or a newly acquired shared lease. The legacy acquisition paths keep
their existing behavior.

Local text-source acquisition, structured filter resolution and text-statistics
analysis acquisition use this path with the original request's borrowed phase.
Tests cover a real scheduler with one ordinary CPU slot (the waiting writer
releases CPU so its lock holder can resume), unchanged operation/byte ownership,
simulated timed waits and rejection, failed CPU resumption, the production text
adapter, and all prior lock cancellation/fairness/wakeup regressions.
`zig build antfly-controlled-service-lock-test antfly-text-scoring-authority-test`
provides focused correctness evidence. Controlled exclusive acquisition still
needs adoption across production writers and other service fences. CPU yielding
inside lock-holding query work remains unqualified until the complete lock/wait
dependency graph permits resumption and control progress; these tests do not
prove the broader runtime resource/performance/default gates.

Native batch admission now has a synchronous original-owner contract through
`DB.batchWithAdmissionControls`. It checks the caller at entry and carries the
same lifetime and optional CPU wait boundary into snapshot mutation admission
and exclusive apply acquisition. Portable-runtime gates still run before and
after apply acquisition. An existing mutation lease is explicitly retained,
including capture-owned helper borrows, rather than reentering reader admission
behind a queued capture. Admission controls stop at those pre-decision fences;
primary durability, mandatory retirement and post-commit visibility retain their
existing distinct contracts.

Focused snapshot tests use a real scheduler with one ordinary CPU slot, exercise
both mutation/capture wait directions, preserve operation/byte ownership and
exactly-once lease release, and reject expired/canceled/closed nested retains.
Native focused snapshot/lock and text regressions passed 57 tests within the
3 GiB compiler bound. A separate `antfly-mutation-service-admission-test`
exercises the actual DB batch entry, every observed admission checkpoint,
absence of rejected documents, release of both service fences and successful
reuse. That production test and full storage integration are queued and have
not yet qualified this wiring. Serving/ABI write callers still need to transport
this original-owner contract; other writer/maintenance/catalog waits and the
full lock dependency graph remain unfinished. These changes do not enable CPU
yielding inside pinned query work or automatic pooling defaults.

Bound one-table, predicate-free commit batches now pass the existing commit
team borrow and original pre-decision context into native mutation admission.
The same-process `TableWriteSource` control callback retains that team until the
synchronous batch returns; no new callback capability or serialized authority
is introduced. The shared admission adapter checks lifetime without CPU yielding,
uses the supplied pre-decision clock directly, and parks/resumes the original
borrow at contended snapshot/apply waits. Resumption captures the current class
instead of assuming the parent class. Post-durability visibility keeps its own
cancellation token. The pre-decision error remains distinct for proven
pre-proposal expiry.

Focused adapter tests cover unrelated service/original clock domains, sticky
expiry/cancellation, missing borrowed lifetime support, original cancellation
while parked, failed CPU resumption, captured-class restoration and service-fence
retirement. Together with snapshot/lock/text regressions, 59 native tests passed
within the 3 GiB compiler bound. The physical bound-source regression is included
in `antfly-local-commit-control-test` and queued with the cumulative storage/ABI
run; it has not yet qualified production wiring. Guarded and explicit transaction
admission, provisioned/Raft writer paths, durable completion waits and the remaining
lock dependency graph still need adoption. Lock-held query CPU yielding and
automatic defaults remain unqualified.

Guarded and explicit bound transaction commits now keep one original admission
budget through BEGIN, intent preparation and preparation retries. Native DB
entry points accept borrowed controls for those pre-decision apply waits; batches
and transaction admission share the same portable-runtime gate recheck after
CPU resumption. Bound preparation checks the retained budget again after intent
acceptance, so rejection still enters the existing durable abort and participant
acknowledgement path. Replicated replay, commit decisions, abort and resolution
retain their existing independent completion behavior.

Group-local BEGIN/prepare callbacks now retain their supplied pre-decision clock
and cancellation while acquiring apply. Those callback contracts do not carry a
runnable borrow, so their CPU-owner transport remains unfinished. This change
also does not qualify CPU yielding inside transaction preparation or pinned
queries, provider/storage I/O, other row-policy/replication/catalog waits or
mandatory completion waits.

The shared apply-admission tests use a real single ordinary CPU slot, observe
unchanged operations/retained bytes while parked, and prove a late activation
gate rejection releases the acquired fence. Original cancellation/expiry/closed
rejections and missing-Io admission preserve reusable legacy fences. Together
with the prior adapter, snapshot/lock and text tests, 61 native focused tests
passed within the 3 GiB bound. Physical tests cover every observed BEGIN/prepare
admission checkpoint and a bound transaction whose original lifetime rejects
after durable BEGIN but must still abort and release intents; those tests remain
queued in `antfly-mutation-service-admission-test` and
`antfly-local-commit-control-test`, not yet production qualification. The full
storage/ABI integration, real overload/resource/performance matrix and automatic
defaults remain unqualified.

Active write completion can now create independently scheduled children from a
quiescent, single-slot parent. Children inherit the already accepted finite
completion authority, class and original clock; they cannot reserve a new
completion/cleanup fence or promote capacity. The validated child factory may
continue that bounded completion family after scheduler close, while new roots
remain rejected. Operation and byte partitions still apply before publication,
and every child must physically retire before its parent finishes. Cleanup
roots and inactive completion authority remain outside this child capability.
The write-completion bridge exposes this factory through the existing child ABI;
a wider whole team must first shrink to its coordinator slot.

Child creation also preserves an implicit parent Io clock explicitly before
installing the independent worker Io. Both foreground and completion children
therefore keep the original deadline domain, including when worker clocks differ.
Completion options retain the child's charged bytes and worker lane without
refreshing its inherited deadline.

All 52 native scheduler tests, shared admission/lock/snapshot adapters, native
text regressions and 8 write-team bridge tests passed: 121 native tests within
the declared compiler bounds. Tests cover close, original foreground expiry,
finite completion expiry, operation/byte exhaustion, denied wider-team receiver
retirement, cleanup/extension rejection, original clocks and final zero ownership.
Pinned Nix/glibc Linux and cumulative physical storage/ABI validation are queued
for this revision. Participant fanout still needs independently owned children,
per-call group control transport and mandatory joins; shared coordinator borrows
must not be forwarded into concurrent workers. Broad wait/body coverage, real
resource/overload/performance gates and automatic defaults remain unfinished.

Participant pre-decision contexts now carry an optional process-local runnable
borrow. It belongs to one participant call and must remain alive through that
call and its physical consumers; parallel calls must receive independent child
owners. Deadline translation preserves this token. The compiled table-write
boundary forwards it through aware BEGIN/prepare callbacks and rejects legacy
fallback even when the token lacks a lifetime callback. Native bound BEGIN and
prepare construct their controlled admission budget from this token, releasing
and reacquiring its captured write class at service-lock waits while retaining
the original portable deadline/cancellation. Initial setup gates consult its
non-yielding lifetime callback and preserve the original rejection cause.

Provisioned group-local owner forwarding now preserves the entire pre-decision
context rather than invoking legacy BEGIN/prepare callbacks. The direct-open
fallback rejects a supplied token until its physical wait graph is controlled.
This does not yet enable participant fanout: the coordinator must still reserve
independent children, park across physical joins, and pass each child's borrow
through per-call worker contexts and remote waits. Restore/Raft and other
provisioned service waits still need complete dependency coverage.

Native focused qualification covers 128 tests across scheduler/service admission,
text authority, completion teams and compiled table-write contracts. The final
run executed 92 tests and reused 36 unchanged successful tests; earlier runs and
an environmental NoSpaceLeft failure are preserved with its receipt. Pinned
Nix/glibc Linux and cumulative physical storage/serving validation are queued
separately. These focused results do not qualify automatic defaults or the
resource/performance matrix.

The independently scheduled participant window now reserves every stable child
packet before task publication, parks the coordinator in its captured class,
and physically joins the group before attempting coordinator resumption. Child
receivers and operation/byte charges survive a denied resumption; retirement
follows the physical join and destruction of each worker arena. Partial window
reservation rolls back all unpublished children and bounded allocations.
`Team.reserveIndependent` shrinks a quiescent ordinary team to one coordinator
slot without requesting simultaneous CPU capacity for its participant window.
Protected control teams reject this mode, including attempts to construct a
window after a legacy team reservation, so independent children cannot widen
terminal work into the health reserve. Completion children expose the remaining
budget from their inherited original clock; observing it grants no fresh time.

Native qualification covers 134 selected tests: the final run executed all 14
SQL team/window tests and reused 120 unchanged successful tests. Real physical
workers demonstrate two independent completion children at one ordinary CPU
slot, original foreground cancellation/expiry, scheduler close, protected
health progress, deadline rejection after physical join, exact arena/receiver
retirement, operation/byte/allocator rollback, and quiescent grant shrinking.
Current pinned Nix/glibc Linux and cumulative physical integration remain
separate qualifications. The participant coordinator has not yet adopted this
window; per-call hosted/local worker binding, remote wait/budget propagation and
all four BEGIN/prepare/commit/abort phases still need that production wiring.
Automatic defaults and the resource/performance matrix remain unqualified.

The distributed transaction coordinator now adopts independently scheduled
participant windows for capable local/hosted workers with active finite
completion authority. It shrinks to one coordinator CPU slot, allocates a
bounded packet array and reserves every packet before the first coordinator
BEGIN. Registry reservation initially leaves children resource-blocked rather
than eligible for CPU: an unused packet cannot consume the only ordinary slot.
Each physical worker activates its own packet. BEGIN, prepare, committed
follower resolution and abort follower resolution park the coordinator, destroy
worker arenas, physically join, then resume the original coordinator class.

Packets retain their original receiver, completion clock and operation/byte
charges across windows and phases. They may reactivate only after their owning
window joins; no new coordination allocation or child admission follows the
durable decision. Failed resumption retains the original cause, rejects further
coordinator callbacks and reports committed propagation debt. Denied initial
child reservation retires partial ownership and finishes the reserved team
before any participant contact.

Local BEGIN/prepare forward each call's independent borrow through the compiled
admission boundary without mutating shared worker context. Hosted calls use a
stack-local view and remote wait boundary; committed resolution translates the
remaining original completion budget conservatively and retains the supplied
post-commit cancellation token. Local resolution carries the original lifetime
through its cancellation boundary, but its complete durable service-wait graph
still needs runnable control transport. Coordinator status/acknowledgement and
ambiguous-decision recovery also need complete scoped wait coverage.

Native qualification passes 156 selected tests: 147 coordinator/window,
scheduler/service-lock, compiled write-contract and text checks, plus 9 existing
child-owner/native-borrow regressions. Coverage includes an actual coordinator
invocation, admission denial before any RPC, all four phase helpers, repeated
physical packet reuse, unused-packet single-slot progress, original completion
expiry, failed resumption and protected health progress. Hosted RPC routing and
physical durable storage waits are not qualified by the mock coordinator tests.
Pinned Nix/glibc Linux and cumulative physical integration are separate gates.
The full resource/overload/performance matrix and automatic defaults remain
unqualified.

Coordinator status, single/bulk acknowledgement and ambiguous decision retries
now dispatch through execution-aware callbacks when an invocation owns a
runnable borrow. Incapable callbacks cannot fall back to an unscoped legacy RPC.
Hosted workers construct call-local remote wait boundaries and cap status,
resolve-retry and acknowledgement timeouts by the original finite completion
budget, additionally respecting a shorter recovery deadline. Mixed-version
bulk ACK fallback uses the same authority for each single ACK; uncertain batch
outcomes retain recovery debt without claiming single deliveries. Shared hosted
worker state remains unchanged. Recovery backoff parks the captured coordinator
class and always attempts the original resumption before proceeding.

Local coordinator callbacks retain original lifetime checks before/after calls
and pass finite deadlines to existing bounded status/resolve APIs. ACK helpers
now check supplied cancellation around ordinary as well as restore operations.
These local adapters still hold CPU across internal physical waits: completing
the storage/Raft service-wait dependency graph remains required, and parking
around an entire local operation would leave CPU work unscheduled. Routing,
credentials and complete physical HTTP dependency coverage also remain open.

Latest-main integration exposed stale source-profile bindings. The generated
control catalog now includes shared relational activation/recovery contracts and
excludes physical C API implementation imports. Its generator normalizes blank
sections so regeneration remains stable under Zig formatting. A physical DB
admission fixture explicitly binds its decoder-cache DB owner. Control-only
aggregation rejects a native DB shortcut before instantiating that physical
helper; aggregation continues through the control profile's query kernel.

Relational activation fixtures that open physical DBs now belong to the physical
owner suite. Control consumers retain guarded failure-publication, bounded
admission and typed coverage-identity tests. The independent relational contract
root references recovery declarations and runs those control tests without
importing a physical DB; the literal ownership audit includes both this root
and the participant fanout control root. Focused native coverage passes 16
relational/participant tests, and the compilation accounting/ownership tool has
12 passing checks using Zig 0.17. Complete physical integration is still required
to qualify these bindings and physical mutation/activation behavior. Runtime,
resource/performance and automatic default gates remain open.

Pre-decision batch admission now carries its original controls through the
process-wide replication mutation barrier before snapshot/apply admission. The
controlled shared and exclusive barrier APIs park only while acquiring a lease,
then require CPU reacquisition before proceeding. Exclusive acquisition closes
new reader admission while waiting for existing mutations, and rejection releases
that capture intent. Nested shared acquisition retains the original physical
lease and checks the same lifetime without creating another execution owner.

The focused native scheduler fixture exercises both directions with one ordinary
CPU slot, protected health progress, cancellation, original-clock deadline expiry
and scheduler shutdown, checking barrier reuse and retained operation/byte charges
through physical joining. Production capture callers and durable local resolve
still need execution-control transport and their complete service-wait dependency
graph; these APIs alone do not qualify that graph or automatic defaults.

Local transaction resolution now forwards the original completion cancellation
token through the provisioned source's local owner handoff. The compiled table
write boundary checks the token before dispatch and refuses legacy resolution
fallback when any token component is supplied. Unscoped callers retain legacy
compatibility. Contract coverage uses both direct and private ABI dispatch,
including expiry during the callback, rejection before a subsequent call and
atomic cancellation. This closes an authority loss, but does not release CPU
across the internal storage, Raft, catalog or group-admission waits.

Provisioned local BEGIN and PREPARE now retain their original budget through
group-operation admission, including retirement, structural/read/status owners
and transition/candidate preparation fences. Controlled condition waits poll
with owner Io, release CPU using the original captured class when available,
and release the activity mutex before mandatory CPU resumption. Rejection returns
with that mutex held so registered waiter accounting is removed under the same
lock. Resolution admission checks its supplied completion cancellation token
through the same bounded physical waits; it does not yet transport a runnable
borrow for CPU release. Unscoped callers retain notification-driven legacy waits.

Focused helper coverage verifies unlocked CPU reentry, rejection cleanup lock
ownership, original-clock deadline expiry and sticky cancellation. These checks
do not instantiate the physical provisioned source's admission state machine;
its full integration, complete local completion/capture wait graph and automatic
default qualification remain open.

Local resolution now has an explicit process-local execution callback at the
compiled table-write boundary. Local workers and hosted workers that resolve
to a local route carry the original runnable and completion cancellation to
that callback without reconstructing a foreground deadline. Provisioned sources
use it during group admission and forward it to their local owners. Hosted
control sources retain it through delegation; physical hosted sources keep the
context on their fenced batch route. Bound ordinary sources check it before
entering native resolution, retaining the synchronous caller through return.

The private ABI contract rejects incapable resolution callbacks without falling

### Checked original CPU reentry

Runnable ABI version 12 adds a synchronous, non-yielding restriction to return
CPU on an already admitted execution. The scheduler checks it outside its mutex
before queueing, during the existing finite CPU wait, and before returning a
grant. Checks use the caller's original clocks/cancellation and can only tighten
its lifetime. They create no root, reservation, deadline or completion authority.
A rejected queued or just-granted execution stops and releases its CPU/queue
position; physical operation and byte charges remain until owning finish.

Read, local child, write completion, cleanup, SQL and archive owner adapters
transport the restriction without retaining it. Native borrowing forwards it
through the ABI back to the owning scheduler. Controlled budgets use checked
return when the owner supports it. Routed admission requires support before
parking and refuses incapable owners rather than entering an unbounded fallback.
Its independent fence/catalog restriction now applies while waiting for CPU,
closing the preceding route-subdeadline gap. Existing unscoped operation and
legacy optional owners retain their prior paths; automatic defaults still require
full adoption and proof rather than treating compatibility as qualification.

### Shared SQL executor observability and node saturation

SQL execution, control and cleanup roles now expose configured capacity, retained
capacity, consumer count, peak consumers, retirement, successful acquisitions and
rejections. Metadata and data health metrics use the same formatter with a bounded
`role` label. Retained capacity includes physical executor retirement even after
the last consumer leaves. Each role snapshot is coherent under its own mutex;
aggregate worker counters and separate role snapshots are not transactional.
These counts describe executor ownership, not runnable CPU occupancy, queue depth
or query admission. Borrowed runtimes and unsupported small worker envelopes
report zero shared-role capacity. Reopening an executor preserves node counters.

The focused shared SQL suite exercises thirty-two imported execution consumers
with one eleven-slot executor. Eleven execution callbacks and eight cleanup
callbacks physically block, an additional submission to either saturated role
fails, and a control callback completes. Releasing idle peers preserves the active
consumers and all twenty-four role reservations. Every physical callback is
joined before its consumer releases; final release recovers all worker gates and
reservations. The test also checks reservation failure, invalid requested sizes,
metrics text, peak consumer accounting and executor reopening.

This suite instantiates real native executors and capability receivers, but no
physical DB, HTTP server or pgwire session. It does not establish node-wide fair
CPU adoption, end-to-end query correctness, defaults, resource envelopes or
performance qualification. Full cumulative integration remains required for the
physical shared-runtime SQL case and the health-source call sites.

### Original lifetime through replication startup recovery

A physical cumulative local commit-control test stalled in replication startup
recovery before reaching its intended snapshot-owned apply wait. The captured
all-thread backtrace identified the uncancelable startup apply acquisition. Its
test lifetime callback only rejected after snapshot capture, which startup
recovery had not yet reached. The exact test process was terminated after the
backtrace was preserved; the compiler and controller continued. That run is
failed evidence, not a passing or timed-out qualification.

Pre-decision batch writes now pass their original lifetime into startup recovery,
its flush mutex, initial durable-outbox scan and final ordered apply fence.
Rejection preserves pending startup/policy flags and undelivered outbox entries.
Each recovery delivery checks admission before starting; successful delivery
still performs mandatory durable acknowledgement before observing rejection for
the next entry. Legacy and mandatory completion callers retain their existing
uncontrolled wrappers. CPU remains retained inside the service holder graph;
mandatory CPU reentry adoption and provider physical deadlines are still open.
Outbox page materialization and delivery/acknowledgement work are not made bounded
by these acquisition checks.

The existing snapshot-owned fixture explicitly completes startup recovery before
holding apply, so it reaches the phase its callback measures. A new physical DB
fixture separately covers startup flush/apply contention, deadline, cancellation
and scheduler closure, no partial write, retained startup obligations and healthy
retry. Both physical fixtures require cumulative integration. The small focused
suite exercises the actual shared startup helper with real IO mutex and apply
rw-locks in six rejection/retry scenarios, using stand-in recovery callbacks;
it does not instantiate a DB or prove provider delivery/durable acknowledgement.

### Admitted durable-outbox page materialization

Pre-decision startup recovery now carries the original synchronous read-admission
port into the physical DocStore snapshot, singleton point batch, cursor seek and
page iteration. Legacy recovery still uses its existing read wrapper. Controlled
reads own one consistent snapshot while the caller holds apply, copy no more than
sixteen mutation obligations, and check the original lifetime between 64 KiB
payload-copy chunks. Partial pages, cursors and readers retire on every rejection
or allocation failure. Reading never clears or publishes an outbox obligation;
the existing delivery/mandatory acknowledgement path is unchanged.

Memory-backed stores now implement admitted read snapshots, point batches and
forward cursor operations. Snapshot admission waits cooperatively on the actual
backend mutex; rejection after retaining a snapshot rolls that reference back
before unlocking. Rejected point batches clear borrowed output slots. The memory
backend originally rejected this read capability with ExecutionWaitUnsupported;
no uncontrolled fallback was added to conceal that boundary.

The six focused checks include the two existing storage page/cleanup fixtures,
large-payload checked copies, allocation failure, every observed lifetime
checkpoint for cancellation/deadline/scheduler closure, and held payload-policy
and memory-backend reader gates. They use a real DocStore and persistent memory
backend, checking exact pending entries, singleton contents, unrelated data and
snapshot reference recovery. They instantiate no physical DB/API/provider. LSM
cold-reader integration, full production startup callers, provider deadlines,
mandatory acknowledgement latency, overall memory accounting and fair CPU holder
adoption remain separate open requirements. The copy quantum bounds local memcpy
between checks; it does not bound allocation, snapshot construction, tree key
comparison or foreign I/O latency.

### Read-budget lifetime restrictions during checked CPU return

The earlier cumulative text-statistics binary reproduced nine
InvalidRunnableTransition failures (40/49 checks passed). Shared read budgets
called their ordinary CPU checkpoint from a checked-reentry restriction while
the original execution was parked or queued. A running checkpoint correctly
rejects that state, so the adapter prevented valid reads from resuming.

While a budget owns a parked phase, it now checks the original borrow's retained
lifetime and calls the request-specific restriction with a temporary controls
copy whose CPU borrow is absent. The stored controls, parent, phase, original
clock/deadline and physical resources remain owned. This permits restrictions
before queue admission and after a grant without CPU checkpoints or yielding
inside enterChecked. Once return succeeds, running checkpoints retain their
ordinary behavior. Missing retained-lifetime capability rejects before parking;
original rejection remains sticky until owning physical retirement.

The trusted-control suite retains its existing physical file/descriptor/async
read, credit, cache and cleanup fixtures. New cases reject both queued and
post-grant restrictions, verify retained operation/bytes/deadline/class, observe
control progress, and verify missing-capability rejection without releasing CPU.
All fifty-one trusted checks passed on the compiled native binary with loopback
permission; the initial sandbox run's remaining decision-transport failure is
preserved separately. The transport fixture uses a loopback test server, not a
production deployment. Full generic-helper consumers, independent archives,
physical DB/API integration, provider deadlines, background holder adoption and
runtime/performance/default qualification still require their own evidence.


### Fresh HA capture ownership during rejected CPU return

Authenticated HA fence and seed-capture requests now acquire the mutation
barrier as fresh operations. Another Io operation can own a legacy shared
mutation lease on the same OS thread; its thread-local nesting marker does not
authorize or reject this capture. Existing nested callers retain the guarded
shared-to-exclusive upgrade path. Acquisition preserves the original execution
and deadline, holds writer intent while CPU is parked, and releases that intent
and its reader gate on rejection without releasing another operation's lease.

The focused HA regression uses the actual barrier, scheduler and ingress
admission adapter with one ordinary CPU and a separate protected control lane.
It checks successful same-thread contention and cancellation, original expiry,
scheduler closure and denied CPU return after parking. The mutation remains
physically held on every rejected path; health progresses, capture and holder
metadata/bytes remain owned until their respective finishes, and the first
failure remains sticky after clearing its trigger. Legacy nested upgrade
rejection and barrier reuse are checked separately.

This qualifies fresh capture admission, not CPU transfer inside the retained
HA state/cache/native snapshot holder graph. Those holders still use original
non-yielding lifetime checks while retaining CPU. Legacy shared leases retain
thread-local nesting and same-thread release requirements. Production background
holder adoption, physical syscall bounds, full archive/API/DB integration,
resource envelopes, performance and default sizing remain open requirements.

The cumulative SQL runner crashed in the physical spill-creation fixture after

A focused gate runs the existing physical spill cases, including successful

Full SQL corpus/independent consumer integration, production physical I/O bounds

### Original graph cleanup pass lifetime

Recurring graph endpoint cleanup previously supplied no original lifetime to
its callback, backfill apply acquisition or mutation pipeline. Each scheduled
pass now owns a shutdown flag and one finite ten-second deadline from callback
entry. The callback borrows a non-yielding lifetime authority; backfill apply
and queued mutation admission use that same authority, without a refreshed
clock or deadline. Entry/return fences preserve the exact expiry cause through
boolean/provider errors and reject swallowed expiry. Accepted mutations retain
the existing mandatory durability and cleanup path.

The focused owner fixture holds a real apply reader, rejects cleanup's queued

A physical DB fixture separately checks retained durable cleanup obligations
after apply rejection and exactly-once healthy retry. That DB fixture requires
the cumulative producer-maintenance gate; the focused owner gate does not
instantiate a DB or prove production mutation completion.

This extends bounded pre-decision waiting. It does not admit callback CPU stages
or make provider reads, graph backfill transactions and durable commits
physically interruptible. Metadata/authority reads before apply still require
controlled reader adoption; the retained service-holder graph still requires

The rotated pressure matrix previously launched candidate fail-fast but omitted

### Operation-owned mutation root migration: lease primitive

`MutationBarrier.acquireSharedRootControlled` now returns a distinct
`RootSharedLease` that owns one physical reader independently of thread-local
legacy nesting. Its release can run on another worker after physical joining.
It retains original acquisition controls, writer admission priority and final
rejection rollback. Legacy `SharedLease` callers and nesting are unchanged.

Two focused fixtures cover same-thread distinct operations at C1/H1, cross-worker
physical release, genuine legacy nesting after that release, root/byte ownership
through caller retirement, and the original deadline across CPU parking while
a reader and the writer gate remain held. The two fixtures also exercise legacy
nesting and capture exclusion; runtime-library tests are not independently
discovered through this consumer root and are not counted. These checks qualify
the primitive only, not production adoption.

The migration must next propagate explicit enclosing root scope through
`BatchExecutionContext`, `BatchExecutionOptions`, synchronous mutation/recovery
receivers, nested DB helpers and commit/resolution cleanup. Nested work must
borrow its root rather than reacquire behind a queued writer. Root release stays
before remote durability waits after the replication record is complete, and
accepted work retains its separate completion authority. No production outer
lease is switched until that complete graph is wired and physically verified.
`retainedLeaseControls` still prohibits CPU transfer inside unconverted holders;
this work does not enable defaults or qualify whole-holder CPU lending.


### Explicit enclosing mutation borrows

`RootSharedLease` now lends `SharedLease` consumers an explicit root pointer.
Borrow acquisition increments an atomic count without entering the writer gate
or changing legacy thread-local nesting. Controlled borrowing checks the original
non-yielding lifetime before and after acquisition; post-acquisition rejection
rolls back only that borrow. Borrow release can run on another worker. The root
must remain at a stable address until every borrower physically joins and
releases; root release asserts that the count is zero.

`BatchExecutionOptions`, `BatchExecutionContext` and synchronous recovery
`Context`/`Execution` carry the borrowed root. Prepared batch admission and its
replication/change-record/pressure contexts preserve an explicitly supplied
scope. Receiver-based nested mutation helpers and context-based DB helpers
borrow it when present. Controlled admission rejects a root belonging to another
barrier. No root pointer is installed on the shared resident DB.

Four consumer fixtures exercise the preceding two root checks plus borrowing
under a held writer gate with cross-worker release, and entry/post-grant
Canceled/DeadlineExceeded/SchedulerClosed/Forbidden rejection with an existing
borrow retained. These are primitive/admission checks; they do not execute the
full DB batch or recovery receiver. The cumulative consumer suite must validate
those implementations separately.

Production callers still use legacy outer leases. Specialized batch dispatch,
transaction/resolution entry, nested materialization and post-commit cleanup
must propagate enclosing scope completely before replacing those outer leases.
The dedicated recovery receiver cannot replace ordinary DB batch callbacks,
which retain resident completion behavior. Mandatory completion authority and
release before remote durability waits remain requirements. CPU transfer inside
retained service holders and pooling defaults remain disabled/unqualified.

The one-shot DB recovery pass checks write policy at entry without holding a

Two focused tests execute the production notification loop against an actual

The actual DB integration fixture also binds a real replication mutation barrier

All ongoing implementation uses `.worktrees/workload-scheduling` on

### Transaction resolution retires enclosing mutation readers

The resolver passes a stable nullable lease slot to its prepared batch. After
primary commit and the corresponding replication tails are locally ordered, the
batch retires its nested reader and then the resolver reader before remote
acknowledgement, derived visibility, and resident graph cleanup. Optimistic
precommit failures retain the enclosing reader. Retirement is idempotent and
cannot be canceled or acquire another execution owner.

Both no-intents retry paths use the same handoff. Outstanding transaction
outboxes append all local tails under transition/capture protection, then release
that protection before remote completion. Each outbox is acknowledged and cleared
separately, preserving uncertain-delivery debt and partial completion. Persistent
cleanup reacquires a mutation reader before the apply lock and rechecks authority.

The focused mutation-root consumer has five checks, including nested resolver/
batch retirement with C1/H1 capture and the original operation/bytes retained.
The actual HA transaction retry fixture now requires physical capture during the
initial lost reply and the no-intents retry, and checks durable debt before and
after acknowledgement. That fixture remains unqualified until the cumulative
hot-standby gate runs. This is direct resolver/batch retirement, not complete
operation-root migration or CPU lending throughout every enclosing service
holder. Full integration, broader ownership migration, resource/performance
qualification, and enabling defaults remain required.

The resident cleanup pass's directory-migration branch now acquires mutation

### Outbox deletion checks authority after apply acquisition

Both normal batch completion and the idempotent transaction-outbox completion
path recheck replication write authority after taking the cleanup apply lock.
Waiting for that lock cannot carry an earlier authority check into deletion
under a subsequently fenced generation. Failed authority retains durable debt.

The server DB integration suite now includes actual no-intents resolver cases
with both batch and replay outboxes: replay reply loss clears only the proven

### Startup and durable-outbox recovery separate capture phases

Prepared batches run startup recovery before acquiring their primary mutation
reader. A directly enclosing resolver reader is released for that startup phase
and reacquired with the original controls before preparation continues. Restore-
scoped resolution likewise flushes earlier durable obligations before acquiring
its own mutation reader. No new operation or deadline is created.

The local durable recovery helper acquires mutation protection before matching
or appending a record under transition/log ordering. It releases transition and
its local reader before remote completion and final write-authority checking.
Context projection preserves the common barrier even when an individual mirror
omits its own binding, and rejects a root from another barrier before publication.
Generic durable-outbox deletion independently reacquires mutation/apply protection
and checks captured replication policy after apply. The pending-append flag being
repaired cannot reject its own cleanup.

Focused recovery checks exercise protected appends, physically joined capture
workers during successful/fenced/uncertain completion, original rejection at a
held capture with reader rollback, common mirror bindings, and wrong-root
rejection. The actual HA recovery fixture also covers a following batch draining
the startup barrier, without duplicating an already appended mutation. That DB
fixture, resolver reacquisition, and full consumer instantiations remain pending
cumulative integration. An externally owned explicit root or any unconverted
coarse holder still requires phase migration; retained service-holder controls
continue to suppress CPU lending. Whole scheduler/memory/lifetime/performance
qualification and default enablement remain incomplete.


### Invocation-owned startup recovery scope

Startup admission accepts a stable borrowed mutation root from batch options.
Both flush phases preserve it through each recovery context and final debt
cleanup, rather than reacquiring an unrelated reader behind writer intent.
Receiver-based entry points retain their previous behavior, including dedicated
local recovery contexts; no root pointer is written to the shared resident DB.

A focused startup fixture holds the writer gate while an explicit physical root
remains live. Both flush phases borrow that exact root, create no pending reader
or CPU wait, and retire every borrow before the enclosing root is released.
The existing startup lifetime/rejection fixtures and outbox recovery checks
remain in their respective gates. Actual DB option/context propagation and
cleanup still require cumulative integration. This preserves nested ownership;
it does not retire a caller-owned root for remote waits, adopt CPU lending, or
qualify defaults.

The canonical worktree now owns its untracked immutable Zig package cache.
The previous symlink to a removed historical task cache was repaired using a
verified local copy; the running historical validator points to the canonical
cache without tracked source or HEAD changes.


### Stable-address mutation root phases

An explicitly owned mutation root can retire its physical reader while retaining
its stable address and barrier identity. Retirement is idempotent, rejects active
borrows, and does not consult cancellation or create execution ownership.
Reentry acquires an independent reader with the supplied original controls and
writer priority. Entry/post-grant rejection leaves the root retired; final release
works in either phase without double unlocking. Controlled borrowing rejects a
retired phase rather than using an invalid physical lease.

The enclosing owner must physically join every borrower and serialize transitions
against new borrow attempts. A zero borrow count does not prove those joins. The
phase flag is owner-managed under that contract, not an admission protocol for
concurrent phase transition and borrowing. CPU authority must be resumed before
reentry acquires a new service reader.

Eight focused root checks now include joined cross-worker borrower release,
retirement/C1 parking/H1 capture with the original operation and bytes retained,
fresh reentry alongside another operation's legacy reader, and original entry/
post-grant rejection with physical reader rollback and healthy reuse. These are
root primitive checks. Production callers still need explicit phase adoption,
complete service-holder migration and actual DB/consumer validation before CPU
lending or defaults can be enabled.

### Scoped mutation phase ownership

An invocation may initialize a stable mutation root in its retired state. Scoped
admission and durable recovery open a physical phase using the original lifetime
controls. The guard that opens that phase owns its retirement; nested guards only
borrow and cannot retire an already-held caller phase. Releasing the opening guard
after all borrowers physically join drops the reader while preserving the root
identity for later cleanup. Entry, post-grant and borrow rejection roll back both
the reader and borrow count. Mandatory self/context helpers can open retired roots
without inheriting another operation's legacy thread-local reader.

Durable recovery releases its locally owned phase after append and transition
release, before remote completion. The recovery consumer check verifies actual
joined capture during completion, final fencing rejection, and uncertain reply
preservation. Eleven mutation-root and fourteen recovery checks pass natively.
Full consumer/DB validation remains queued. Production outer entries still need
complete invocation root propagation through resident DB helpers before switching
to fresh roots by default; the dedicated recovery receiver cannot replace resident
DB semantics and maintenance. This change does not enable service-holder CPU
lending or qualify pooling defaults. Enclosing owners must continue to serialize
phase transitions and physically join borrowers before releasing the opening guard.

### Cooperative SQL response serialization and retained read guards

HTTP result, preparation metadata and streamed-row JSON now use a shared compact
encoder under the original execution authority. JSON values use an allocator-owned
iterative frame stack; scans and copies poll in 4 KiB chunks, traversal polls every
64 steps, and buffer/frame growth copies in bounded chunks without remap/realloc.
The response and NULL-flag buffers remain charged to the existing response budget.
Standard compact encoding is preserved, including custom OpenAPI serializers,
exact number strings, invalid UTF-8 byte arrays and optional-field policy.

The HTTP worker retains the adapter's read guard, runnable receiver and connection
owner until result/response work retires. Each output checkpoint revalidates the
guard after a scheduler yield; final publication forces a check. Pgwire's adapter
keeps its existing scoped guard retirement by default. Cancellation and changed
read authority during result encoding use normal SQL diagnostics; completed writes
retain the non-replay acknowledgement diagnostic and encoding-budget failures keep
the existing limit response.

interruption at every observed checkpoint, allocation failure cleanup and 4096
nested JSON values. The shared output-owner fixture checks actual retained guard
pins after repeated scheduler yields and refuses publication after catalog change.
Production HTTP worker fixtures cover result retirement/error classification and
streamed exact integers, text, NUMERIC, arrays and SQL NULLs, with cancellation and
budget exhaustion closing every cursor and retiring leased pages. The production
HTTP route is also type-checked without emitting a binary. Native and pinned
Nix glibc GNU Linux checks pass: 14 reported tests include eight behavioral tests
and six discovery initializers; the companion group contains eight initializers.
Sticky encoder/sink failures prevent custom serializers from swallowing a failed
checkpoint or allocation and publishing partial output.

The controlled array preflight changes below replace legacy counting for the
HTTP stream. Typed input JSON numeric/container work, remaining backend ownership and default
enablement remain work. SQL response copying is covered by the controlled transport
publication changes below. Original-root lifetime through
physical HTTP delivery is covered by the context retirement changes below.

### SQL input authority through physical HTTP response retirement

HTTP SQL input capsules now transfer a reference to the real H1/H2 context before

stable address and pins the node; its final release follows decoded allocations,

transfer. Registration allocation failures roll back the temporary reference.
The route and joined workers drop their own references normally; context teardown
releases the transport reference after response writing and returned response
allocation cleanup, while request input and transport cancellation/Io remain alive.
The original root parks before worker notification and holds no CPU grant during

enqueue, forwarding and response failure paths without creating a replacement root.

### Weighted CPU sharing reserves earned mixed-team capacity

A real scheduler regression exposed a slot-share error under fragmentation: with
2:1 query/write weights, one-slot queries and two-slot writes both continuously
backlogged, the original policy granted 53 queries and 9 writes over the fixture's
interval. Charging writes by their two-slot demand puts this outside the fixture's
bounded tolerance for the configured share. The older all-one-slot sharing test
could not expose the error.

The deficit round now stays open when a backlogged class has enough credit for
its head but none of its queued teams fits the currently free capacity. Running
work drains instead of another class repeatedly taking fragmented slots. The
head receives its existing grant and pays its normal slot cost when it fits.
Same-class small-job backfill retains its existing credit cost and bypass bound;
control/cleanup partition dispatch is unchanged. No owner, queue deadline,
retained-memory reservation or completion authority is replaced.

This intentionally permits temporarily unused ordinary slots to assemble an
already-earned larger team. The mixed-team fixture checks weighted slot grants
while both classes remain backlogged and control admission remains available.
A drain-retirement fixture checks that expired or canceled queued team authority
removes its reservation and immediately admits the smaller queued operation,
with correct retained-byte/operation counts. These are scheduler correctness
fixtures, not wall-clock throughput or whole-node fairness qualification.

Full qualification remains waived and defaults disabled. Whole holder propagation
and CPU reentry, aggregate node accounting, remaining entry-point coverage and
automatic default selection/activation remain unfinished.

### Retained scheduler refusal keeps its original terminal cause

The lower-level retained wait now reads an already-stopped entry's terminal cause
under the scheduler mutex and returns it before invoking later restrictions or
reading a later deadline. Stopping an already-stopped entry no longer overwrites
that cause. This matches the execution wrapper's existing terminal-state contract:
only the owning finish retires the retained operation and bytes. Initial,
unpublished waits preserve their automatic retirement on failure. No CPU grant,
new deadline or completion authority is introduced.

the deadline changed. The fixture now checks both a later deadline and a later
Forbidden restriction, verifies the latter callback is not invoked, preserves
stored cause/count/bytes with zero CPU, admits control work and reconciles all
charges on owning finish. The preserved before-fix receipt records the deadline
counterexample. This verifies terminal scheduler ownership, not physical commit
or whole holder-graph completion.

### Explicit CPU lending around derived visibility polling

VisibilityWait now accepts an optional borrowed execution wait boundary. The
threaded all-index and selected-index paths release the worker mutex before the
physical polling sleep and its boundary callbacks, then restore the mutex on
success or error. A supplied boundary returns CPU before sleeping and must
reenter the original owner before the sleep result or completed visibility can
be consumed. Authority checkpoints preserve the original deadline and causes.
A refused begin performs no sleep or end callback. Existing callers without a
boundary retain CPU, preserving the holder policy until their audits permit
lending; no production post-commit caller is enabled by this change.

### Inline enrichment catch-up retains request authority through unwind

Foreground catch-up now owns an atomic first-rejection slot shared by its copied
provider guards. A fallible request checkpoint stores its original cause and
uses the existing enrichment cancellation signal inside the pipeline. After all
invoked work has joined, the public catch-up method restores the stored original
cause. Repeated checks cannot lose a one-shot rejection or replace it with a
later deadline. The slot remains valid until the synchronous catch-up returns;
active provider guards are restored and existing lane-drain cleanup is retained.

ready-result policy. Enrichment visibility cancellation and timeout are now
recognized by inner control-error decisions, so they bypass provider retry and
terminal-request classification as well as the outer worker supervisor.

already-resolved exit flushes the retained transaction outbox before waiting,
using the existing append/retire/fresh-cleanup sequence rather than bypassing
pending delivery debt. Idempotent outer cleanup remains safe.

budget, and rechecks authority/gate before another physical open/configuration
attempt. CPU acquisition precedes capture reentry; capture waiting can lend again
while no service reader exists. Legacy and private transaction paths keep their

execution admission is required.

### Explicit automatic initial runnable capacity

The platform layer already has general affinity/cgroup CPU and host/container
memory-envelope probes, including fractional quotas and visible ancestors. This
corrects the preceding sizing note, which overlooked that implementation while
inspecting the inference-specific linalg helper. The scheduler now reuses the
general probes for explicit `capacity_mode: "automatic"`. Resolution runs once
before publication, preserving configured slot/byte ceilings and finite operation
and wait limits. The default reserve floor is three runnable lanes, allowing one
ordinary worker plus independent health and cleanup even on fractional CPU
quotas. These lanes share OS CPU time; they are not dedicated physical cores.
Metadata is bounded by the smaller of its configured ceiling and 1/32 of the
visible memory envelope. Too-small envelopes fail policy validation rather than
violating protected metadata headroom. Unknown memory retains the finite ceiling.
Fixed mode and omitted/null scheduling remain unchanged. Existing telemetry
publishes the effective slot and byte policy. This adds explicit initial sizing;
default activation, total process accounting and the remaining design are still
unfinished. The 1/32 metadata share is a conservative initial policy, not a
benchmark-qualified default or a storage/model heap bound.

### Automatic node startup respects the effective process budget

DATA and standalone resolve automatic policy against the smaller of the platform
memory envelope and the effective CLI/environment process budget before creating
the shared node owner. The resolved policy becomes fixed before crossing the
kernel boundary, preserving one effective CPU/metadata envelope for API and
storage consumers. Scheduler initialization also freezes automatic policy before
publication. Fixed operator policy continues unchanged. Unknown host/container
memory still permits a finite configured process budget to constrain metadata;
a budget too small for protected headroom rejects startup. This does not yet
provide aggregate process-heap accounting or enable default scheduling.

scheduling metadata to at most 2 MiB, freezes the effective policy, and remains
unchanged through node owner creation and cleanup-reserve publication. A later
consumer cannot shrink it by invoking resolution with a different resource view.
A 1 MiB automatic budget rejects inadequate control headroom; fixed policy keeps
its original semantics. Full qualification remains waived.

and API pool publication. Automatic mode clamps request and retained-state pools
to each configured ceiling and 1/8 of the effective host/container/process memory
envelope, alongside existing metadata sizing at 1/32. This prevents default
frontend transport/control reservations from independently exceeding a small
process budget. Fixed policies remain unchanged. Unsupported sub-1 MiB pools
reject startup rather than weakening protected reservations. The same resolved
limits reach API allocator pools and outbound service-memory sizing.

generated module changes. Its bytes match the generator output, and the final

### Shared serverless request and autonomous execution owner

OwnedStack now owns a stable optional scheduler and publishes that same pointer
to the HTTP handler and autonomous runtime. Startup validates managed reserves
and establishes cleanup capacity before publishing consumers. Teardown joins
the runtime before closing the scheduler and verifies no operation remains.
Requests retain capacity through response construction and owning finish. Only
bounded healthz/readyz use protected control admission; other routes use ordinary
query/write capacity. Scheduler admission rejection restores the original scoped
guard cause. Background runs acquire before the runtime mutex and retire on
every return. Capacity exhaustion/queue timeout defer a tick instead of poisoning
runtime failure. Inline namespace materialization retains its foreground owner
and does not request a second grant. Graph compute width is capped by ordinary
capacity and charged as a team to writes and autonomous work.

Focused actual handler tests prove health progress under ordinary saturation,
original admission rejection, expiry, closed admission and balanced retirement.
The runtime fixture observes background CPU ownership before cancellation and
verifies zero final CPU/operation/byte charges and no retained runtime mutex.
Bootstrap validation accepts supported policy and rejects insufficient reserves.
This does not yet prove full physical startup, all backend fanout accounting or
CPU lending across serverless waits. Those integrations remain separate work.

without that warning. Source hash comparison proves only the build declaration
changed between behavior and metadata receipts. Linux uses 6 GiB container/5 GiB
compiler bounds; full qualification remains waived and defaults remain disabled.

### Serverless ingest durable acknowledgement boundary

Namespace and table ingest routes now forward the original sticky request guard into Service.ingestBatchWithCancellation. The service checks after encoding and immediately before the first physical WAL append. Once an append accepts the batch, subsequent mutations finish under the admitted ordinary execution and successful 202 responses bypass the final foreground lifetime check. Non-accepted responses still recover the original scoped cause. Existing ingestBatch callers retain the legacy no-cancellation API.

The actual filesystem WAL and HttpHandler regression covers both routes, scheduler enabled/disabled, and Canceled, DeadlineExceeded, SchedulerClosed and CatalogGenerationChanged. Pre-append rejection leaves the original LSN unchanged; rejection after the first physical append still finishes both mutations, returns 202, and retires scheduler operation/CPU/metadata reservations. The existing public-table pending-publication deadline case remains covered.

serverless-durable-ingest-native.json reports four tests plus eight local companions, with unchanged source and external inputs. Its compiler peak 6,117,769,216 bytes exceeded the previous 5 GiB declaration. The target declaration is now 8 GiB; serverless-durable-ingest-memory-native.json passes using cached behavioral code, with only build/api_tests.zig metadata changed between the runs. No Linux verification for this change or full qualification is claimed. Full qualification remains waived and defaults remain disabled.

Accepted multi-record ingestion still retains ordinary CPU until return. Complete durable continuation CPU handoff and all backend wait/fanout propagation remain requirements. Existing per-mutation WAL semantics and response-allocation failure behavior are unchanged; this is not an atomic multi-record ingestion implementation.

### Serverless retained ingest completion and fair checkpoints

Scheduled namespace/table ingestion now reserves the existing independent completion task before possible durable acceptance. A local stable bridge grants only the retained executor and platform monotonic clock. Activation retains the same write root, byte reservation and capacity partition under a finite 30-second completion deadline. The task owns request/service/allocator/execution borrows through physical join. Mutation-loop checkpoints yield ordinary CPU fairly without reusing foreground cancellation or allowing scheduler close to replace the retained fence. Handler error/response recovery observes the retained phase so it cannot overwrite an accepted or ambiguous durable result with a foreground cause.

Ingress charges the task node, joined handle, stable bridge and callback packet before admission. Direct service callers without sufficient root metadata reservation fail before worker/WAL publication. Unscheduled callers retain the previous API and pre-first-append guard behavior.

serverless-durable-completion-metadata-native.json completed with exit 0, unchanged source/external inputs, six tests and eight local companions. The actual Service task on one ordinary slot yields to a queued query between mutations while protected control still runs. The filesystem WAL/HttpHandler regression confirms the retained phase is active during append, both records and the 202 survive actual scheduler close after the first append, and scheduler CPU/operation/metadata ownership retires. Existing scoped rejection tests cover both routes with scheduling enabled/disabled. No Linux rerun or full qualification is claimed; defaults remain disabled.

Physical WAL/provider I/O still retains charged ordinary CPU. Safe loans require retiring backend locks before reentry; unbounded backend calls may exceed the cooperative completion deadline while the owner joins physical work. Comprehensive parser/encoding checkpoints and aggregate memory ownership remain requirements. Existing per-record WAL and response-allocation failure semantics are unchanged.

### Filesystem WAL serialization contention CPU loan

Scheduled ingestion now forwards its retained execution through WalStore.appendWithExecution. Converted filesystem stores use a checked loop before claiming their in-process mutex: checkpoint under ordinary CPU, try the mutex, park without owning any serialization lease, wait one millisecond on the retained executor, reacquire/revalidate the original class and authority, then retry. Denied reentry never owns the mutex or starts physical WAL publication. Providers lacking the optional capability keep charged CPU for their legacy append.

The critical append and cross-process namespace file-lock wait remain charged CPU. No checked CPU reentry occurs while the filesystem serialization lock is held. Backend physical waits, idempotent append, read/latest/truncate propagation and comprehensive memory ownership still need conversion/audit.

serverless-wal-contention-fixed-native.json reports exit 0, unchanged source/external inputs, seven tests and eight local companions. The real filesystem WAL contention fixture proves a query can run on the sole ordinary slot and release a legacy-held store mutex while a writer retains its original metadata reservation. Cancellation, deadline and scheduler-close rejection after the loan leave the physical latest LSN unchanged; success writes the record. The existing retained-completion fixture now intercepts the converted append and still proves actual scheduler closure after acceptance preserves both mutations and 202. Test teardown releases serialization before canceling/joining futures so counterfactual failures terminate.

No Linux rerun or full qualification is claimed; defaults remain disabled. The memory audit also found that filesystem append currently reads/copies the complete existing log. Bounded backend WAL memory remains a concrete requirement before the full design can be considered complete.

### Filesystem WAL bounded working memory

Ordinary and idempotent append now validate existing records with a shared 8 KiB buffered header scanner and copy file ranges into the atomic replacement with 32 KiB scratch. Duplicate operation IDs compare existing payloads in 4 KiB chunks. Recovery uses the same scanner; NEXT_LSN parsing uses a fixed 128-byte buffer. Truncation streams only retained encoded record ranges and preserves next-LSN continuity. Replay scans without materializing the complete log and allocates only selected returned records using the caller allocator. The on-disk record format, namespace serialization and atomic replacement are unchanged.

serverless-wal-streaming-native.json completed with exit 0, unchanged source/external inputs, sixteen tests and eight local companions. A real mixed ordinary/idempotent WAL exceeding 2 MiB is reopened under a 16 KiB requested store-heap budget. Append, duplicate/conflict comparison against a 1 MiB payload, stale sidecar recovery, tail replay, partial/all truncation and subsequent append succeed. Caller-budget replay and new-payload allocation failures release all allocations and leave the latest LSN unchanged. Malformed header/payload/id cases agree with the existing codec and cannot replace the original log. Existing reopen, cross-instance conditional append, idempotency, LSN continuity, CPU contention and accepted-completion tests pass.

This bounds working buffers relative to existing log size; new encoded records and selected returned records remain caller allocations. Atomic append still copies all existing file bytes and can retain CPU throughout critical I/O. Complete aggregate backend/model memory ownership and safe physical wait loans remain requirements. Persistence follows the existing flush/rename semantics, without a power-loss fsync qualification claim. Full qualification remains waived, no Linux rerun is claimed and defaults remain disabled.

These endpoints inspect only fixed runtime state. Diagnostics/catalog/status, non-GET methods and user priority labels remain ordinary. Normalization clamps the reserve to leave one ordinary task; H2 advertised stream capacity follows the normalized task limit. This policy applies even while runnable scheduling is explicitly disabled.

### Serverless process-clamped startup policy and managed lifecycle

Serverless bootstrap resolves automatic runnable policy once before scheduler publication, clamping the platform envelope to its effective process memory budget. Scheduler.init receives a fixed policy, shared at the same stable address by HttpHandler and ManagedRuntime. Explicit fixed policy is not re-probed; null remains rollback. The CLI now accepts --process-memory-budget-mb and uses the common canonical/compatibility environment resolver. Explicit zero requests automatic detection and suppresses inherited malformed values according to the common precedence rules.

Dedicated tests cover freeze/no-reprobe, too-small metadata envelope rejection, null rollback, flag parsing and CLI/canonical/compatibility precedence.

This qualifies the combined filesystem startup scenario and scheduling metadata sizing, not aggregate process heap enforcement or every deployment/provider/model. Bootstrap now freezes automatic CPU, metadata, request-pool and retained-state ceilings with the common AdmissionConfig resolver before publishing consumers. Transport application allocations and aggregate inbound body storage each use at most the resolved request-pool ceiling (automatic: at most one eighth of the shared process/platform envelope). The body limit leaves room for simultaneous encoded/decoded representations and for the ordinary scheduling metadata allowance, including ingress execution and the largest local completion packet. Normalization cannot enlarge the body quota past the envelope. Protected transport application memory retains its independent subquota.

OwnedStack now publishes one stable allocation owner with foreground, protected control and retained partitions. HttpHandler and transport application allocations share the request pool; catalogs, clients, query/build/runtime resources receive the retained allocator. Shutdown joins consumers before retiring all three pools and checks that their charges are zero. Response conversion also frees the content type if body copying fails.

### WAL sidecar memory before publication

Ordinary, idempotent and conditional append now prepare sidecar temporary-path memory before the log replacement can publish a new record. The two decimal u64 fields use a fixed 41-byte inline payload. Partial/all truncation also prepares sidecar memory before replacing/removing the original log. Atomic sidecar writing borrows the prepared path and cleans its temporary file on every exit; it performs no further store-allocator allocation. Next-LSN overflow is checked before append publication.

This eliminates store-heap allocation failures after log publication, not filesystem I/O failures or allocation in the underlying threaded runtime. Existing flush/rename semantics and ambiguous physical I/O outcomes are unchanged. ### Ingest application memory before acceptance

Service now owns the result namespace and all mutation encodings before the first physical WAL append. Encoding checks the original pre-acceptance cancellation and scheduled checkpoints. The append loop keeps its retained completion/checkpoint behavior. The table service transfers the owned namespace into its table result instead of copying after acceptance. Both namespace/table HTTP routes prepare their complete JSON acknowledgement before invoking ingestion. Fixed-width LSN fields use JSON whitespace padding, allowing the accepted LSNs to be filled without allocation or resizing. JSON response construction now frees the content type if serialization fails.

serverless-prepared-ingest-ack-application.json records thirty native tests and nine local companions passing. The unchanged binary passes with localhost access after restricted-sandbox socket failures. Every injected Service allocation failure leaves a real filesystem WAL at LSN zero. A real-WAL interceptor denies all further Service heap allocation after the first record; both mutations and the owned table result still complete and retire all charges. Acknowledgement tests cover every allocation failure, escaped names, zero/max-u64 LSNs, and finishing with a zero-byte allocator budget. Existing both-route accepted-ingest/cancellation/scheduler-close, fairness, transport pressure and managed lifecycle tests remain covered.

Preparing all encodings increases peak application memory, bounded by the shared pool, and can reject a large request before any WAL acceptance. This does not reserve all backend storage for the complete batch or make multi-record append atomic. Backend I/O/allocation failures can retain the existing per-record partial outcome. Transport-neutral response conversion and httpx response construction still allocate after handler return and need ownership/reservation work. Full physical response/wait ownership and protocol/default audits remain requirements. Full qualification remains waived, no Linux rerun is claimed, and scheduling defaults remain disabled.

## Completion audit against the full delivery goal

Current audit: 2026-10-13, codex/workload-scheduling, HEAD d2c629285b (origin/main merged through b77cb634d5) plus the uncommitted implementation. The goal remains sharing bounded execution across many connections by default, preserving sessions, query results, durability and control progress. Focused subsystem receipts do not establish that whole contract.

The user waived full qualification. The large Linux builder, complete performance sweep and full qualification run are not pending blockers or approval gates. Any Linux checks that are run must use pinned Nix glibc Zig. Remaining focused correctness checks must cover the production paths being enabled; historical throughput/latency claims are not inferred from them.

an aggregate budget reset through an unfenced destination. These are modeled
