## Prepaid publication recovery dispatch (2026-10-19)

`native-publication-reserve-v1` connects cooperative publication retries to the recovery
queue/workers allocated before DB mutations can depend on them. Inspection
established that probe/owner storage was already allocated at registration;
there was no missing dynamic probe allocation to fix. The missing use was the
publication owner's submission to the ordinary maintenance executor, which
allocates a job header/future after durable debt may already exist.

Publication owners now accept an optional finite-step callback. Those steps use
the owner's preallocated intrusive recovery slot and the runtime's prepaid
recovery workers. They retain the existing one-flight driver and bounded
successor queue. The callback is bound into each submitted job according to its
class, so a later atomic routing flag cannot change what a reserved job runs.
Registration/runtime construction can still refuse before this resource exists;
this change does not create another task or unbounded queue at completion.

Reserved DB draining requires cooperative publisher admission and completion
polling. The owned native step keeps the existing continuation budget. If it
selects legacy debt or cannot use the owned path, it returns a maintenance marker
before entering legacy full-page/AHO1 materialization. The owner hands that work
to ordinary maintenance after the normal retry interval. Nonpolling publishers
also stay ordinary. Successful ordinary draining restores reserved routing for
later work. Original direct/foreground compatibility methods retain their
existing behavior. Snapshot/provider/allocator costs remain explicit exceptions
to an end-to-end physical CPU bound; an arbitrary callback is not qualified by
its type alone.

Two owner regressions exhaust the parent memory envelope after runtime/owner
registration. Ordinary job allocation is refused, but an accepted finite retry
still runs and retires through the prepaid route. Legacy handoff remains on
ordinary capacity and cannot use the reserve to bypass allocation refusal; it
runs after that pressure is released. A DB regression uses malformed legacy
bytes to prove reserved draining returns the marker before AHO1 decoding,
preserves exact debt and releases its reader. It also rejects a publisher lacking
cooperative recovery. Existing registration-close retirement is now included in
the focused production target alongside actual DB/Primary five-second matching,
ACK preservation, fences, clear/reopen and joined shutdown.

All 284 scoped cases pass: 258 custom-runner plus twenty-six compiled
service/archive/WAL/Primary client cases. All eight native targets and 125
steps pass. AST/formatting checks cover seven changed phase paths. All 4408
exported public files match current sources; the fetched consumer passes 25
semantic steps. Native ABI 22 guards the larger owner/port layouts. Public
C100/private4/memory1/offer3 and persisted formats are unchanged.

Mandatory precommit capacity for all writes and bounded durable obligations,
complete physical memory/resource funding, snapshots/search/allocator/provider
CPU, foreground/legacy continuations, full fairness and default HA fault/restart/
overload/shutdown/post-ACK qualification remain required. Activation/catalog
batching, remaining operators/transports/remote/SDK/Cloud/adaptive policy and the
full scheduler graph remain open. Full Linux qualification stays waived; Linux
builds require pinned Nix glibc Zig.


### Durable ordinary-publication backlog admission (native ABI 23)

Ordinary HA publication now has a per-store durable limit of 4,096 obligations
and 256 MiB of encoded obligation keys and values. DocStore captures changes in
constant space, checks the final atomic batch before primary commit, and writes
an HPB1 aggregate and fixed-size hashed-key size sidecars in that same commit.
Sidecar overhead is bounded separately by the record ceiling. Replacing a record
or deleting and inserting in one batch reuses its credit. A refused batch cannot
commit its source mutations. Abort and an uncertain backend outcome cannot retire
a credit separately from its obligation.

A backend-owned immediate gate prevents overlapping native namespace views from
losing aggregate updates; unrelated writes remain concurrent. It returns
Backpressured instead of parking a worker. Custom single-writer backends use an
owner-local gate. Older roots with outboxes but no aggregate refuse growth until
recovery drains the existing obligations; four keys-only seeks establish the
empty boundary without scanning legacy values. Portable metadata includes neither
the aggregate nor the size sidecars. Native root copies retain their own physical
records. Direct raw backend mutations must preserve the accounting contract.

The six new regressions cover the real count ceiling and atomic source refusal,
byte and arithmetic boundaries, legacy draining, abort and durable reopen,
overlapping namespace views, and backend errors both before and after actual
commit. Uncertain creation and deletion fixtures forbid primary outbox value
reads: cleanup uses the eight-byte size sidecar. The first validation build was
stopped for a confirmed full-value reread regression; its owned-process identity,
termination, and absence are recorded in native-publication-backlog-v1-canceled.json.
The v2 production suites and v3 admission suite passed 290 functional cases.
V2 completed 129/135 native steps, with only the new boundary test failing to
compile because of an implicit integer type. V3 corrects that expression and
passes 60/60 focused native steps. Reversing exactly one expression inside
that previously unselected test reconstructs the v2 source byte for byte; no
production code differs. The v3 build's 5,120 source inputs are exactly current.
The current archive's 4,409 public files match source, and its fetched consumer
passes 25/25 semantic checks. See
`native-publication-backlog-v3-verified.json` and its post-GC receipt in this receipt directory.

This bounds ordinary HA publication debt, not every durable obligation family.
Transaction-specific HA outboxes need publication credit reserved during prepare;
adding refusal only at resolution would be after an irrevocable commit decision.
They remain outside this limit. Node-wide debt policy, configuration and age
metrics, minimum funded completion memory/CPU/I/O/dependencies, bounded cleanup
metadata I/O and index CPU, mixed-version/downgrade accounting, and the full
physical resource graph remain open. The earlier reserved-dispatch proof remains
a dispatch proof, not proof of real database completion under exhausted memory.
The original scheduler design remains incomplete; full Linux qualification stays
waived, and Linux builds must use the pinned Nix glibc Zig toolchain.


### Prepaid local publication envelopes (native ABI 24)

Mandatory batch and replay publication now acquire the native publisher's owned
envelope before the local primary commit. The provider allocates its state and
exact record buffer, copies the payload, and computes its checksum in 4,096-byte
construction quanta under the original lifetime. A present provider's preparation
error refuses the local commit; it cannot fall back to allocating publication.
After commit, sealing writes only the fixed 100-byte header with the publication
LSN. It neither allocates the envelope nor copies or checksums the payload again.
Preparing and abandoning a token consumes no LSN. The token owns its payload,
retains the allocating allocator, permits one publication attempt, and rejects a
changed primary identity. It does not retain the construction Port or cancellation.
Existing log serialization, failure telemetry, deferred acknowledgements and
post-append authority checks remain in the commit owner.

The original lifetime and signed row-policy expiry are checked again after this
preparation, immediately before the local decision. A real DB fixture expires
its lease inside publisher preparation and verifies source-row refusal, no HA
WAL advance, and retirement of the unused envelope. The same fixture proves
that preparation OOM refuses the source, then proves that a successful source
commit can publish its prepaid native envelope while Primary.alloc refuses new
allocations. Its WAL/backend allocators remain funded: this is an envelope-funding
proof, not an exhausted-parent completion proof. Other regressions verify exact
wire bytes, independent payload ownership, every construction refusal quantum,
no LSN on abandonment, stale-identity/single-use rejection, completion after
construction cancellation, and original rejection/cleanup through a foreign
named callback even when a provider ignores rejection or returns a later error.

The complete current source passed 296 functional cases and 135/135
native build steps, including the six durable-backlog regressions. All 5,120
native source inputs are exactly current, with no source-delta exceptions. The
current exported package has 4,409 matching public source files and passes 25/25
fetched-consumer semantic checks. See `native-publication-envelope-v3-verified.json` and its post-GC
receipt under the cumulative integration receipts.

This funds a known local publication envelope. It does not yet prepay WAL/backend
append resources, recovery working memory or every CPU/I/O dependency. Schema,
row-policy and other publication families still need the new preparation path.
Transaction publication credit must be reserved during prepare, before a global
commit decision; local preparation during resolution does not establish that
property. Legacy providers without the new capability retain their existing
publication contract. Whole-node debt policy, the physical resource graph,
bounded end-to-end recovery CPU, default HA qualification and all remaining
requirements of the original scheduler design stay open. Full Linux qualification
remains waived; Linux builds still require the pinned Nix glibc Zig toolchain.


### Metadata and maintenance publication funding (native ABI 25)

Typed and JSON schema setters now prepare mandatory native publication before
constructing and committing the new schema. Row-policy publication prepares its
record before changing the runtime admission gate or committing its preparing
marker. Both policy commit branches consume that same prepared token. The shared
PrimaryReplicationEffect owner also prepares its native frame before committing
physical maintenance effects and their outbox, and retains it through the local
publication attempt. These paths use the same fixed-header publication and owned
payload/checksum contract introduced in ABI 24; wire bytes remain unchanged.

A row-policy outbox is mandatory even when HA acknowledgement policy is async.
Its append failure now propagates through strict metadata publication, reports
DurabilityOutcomeUnknown and retains the exact durable intent. It cannot be
mistaken for optional async delivery and cleared without an append. Legacy
providers without prepare use the same strict fallback for policy delivery;
ordinary optional async schema publication retains its previous failure policy.

Primary.alloc denied for both schema setters. It verifies the old durable/runtime
schema and LSN on refusal, then observes the new schema during publication. The
policy integration fixture proves native preparation OOM leaves the policy gate
disabled and pending marker absent, then injects an async postcommit append error
and verifies a row-policy intent remains until native recovery publishes it. The
existing replica replay, exact Raft receipt and restart checks still run. The
graph-TTL integration fixture injects frame-preparation OOM before retirement and
verifies the source graph and HA LSN remain unchanged, then exercises the existing
postcommit acknowledgement failure and idempotent recovery. A separate strict
async test covers both legacy and prepared failures and caller-owned retirement.

### Transaction batch publication credits at PREPARE (native ABI 26)

A transaction with write intents now reserves its future HA batch outbox in the
same backend batch as its intents and prepared vote. Its durable credit uses the
existing per-DocStore publication pool (4,096 records and 256 MiB), alongside
ordinary outboxes. It reserves one record and an encoded payload bound of six
times the intent-admission bytes plus 64 KiB of fixed envelope allowance. JSON
strings expand at most six bytes per byte; binary metadata byte arrays expand
at most four. The existing admission cost includes per-intent overhead, key
copies, logical values and prepared rows. Tests exercise actual native encoders
with control characters, binary metadata, maximal fixed fields and overflow.
This grant bounds durable batch debt; it is not preallocated encoder or WAL RAM.

The credit is appended before new intents and votes without moving the complete
mutation array. A failed prepare atomically rolls back its credit, vote and
intents. Replacement prepares reuse their existing record. Resolution retains
the credit when it materializes a batch outbox and never requests another debt
grant; delivery acknowledges and deletes the outbox and credit atomically.
Abort and resolution without a batch outbox release the credit. Already-resolved
retries keep their existing delivery ownership and do not need a cold outbox
probe merely to decide whether this resolution creates an obligation.

A durable HTC1 marker fences migration. Before the first tracked prepare, three
keys-only seeks must prove that legacy intents, legacy batch outboxes and stray
credit records are absent. Legacy globally committed transactions can still
materialize and drain their old batch outboxes without obtaining a new grant.
New transaction prepares remain refused until that old debt drains. Credit
updates share the existing native backend publication gate and the same atomic
aggregate/size-sidecar mechanism as ordinary debt. Raw backend mutation can
bypass DocStore admission and is outside this guarantee.

The broader transaction sweep exposed insufficient streaming decoder scratch
funding. With a retained arena and a backing allocator unable to resize in place,
a valid 64 KiB read can require a 196,670-byte backing allocation while the old
logical reservation allowed only 131,136 bytes. The standalone pinned-toolchain
reproducer confirms that refusal. Streaming block readers now fund backing growth
for their two scratch allocations (path and input window), including retained
nodes, before decoding. The bound follows the pinned arena's 1.5x node growth;
output and prefix buffers retain their separate working-space accounting. The
new native regression checks non-resizing backing, allocation failures, physical
charges and retirement. The near-16-MiB prepared transaction can again resolve
across LSM restart at retained-effects quota. The older coalescing test now uses
ReadVersion.preparing and a suspended-lifetime capability, preserving its pinned
layout and expiry assertions rather than referring to removed builder mutexes.

current generated build options. The fetched current public archive matches

The initial active caches disappeared during qualification; fresh caches and

### Prepared WAL encoding before local commit (native ABI 27)

Mandatory prepared HA publication now owns both its replication frame and its
outer WAL encoding before the local source decision. The native WAL grant
captures its allocator, stable WAL identity, immutable tail and checksum state.
Construction copies and checksums payloads in 4 KiB original-control quanta;
refusal or allocation failure retires all partially acquired ownership. The
compiled client restores the original refusal even if a provider ignores it,
and destroys any handle returned alongside that refusal. No request control is
retained by the completed grant. The stable WAL and allocator descriptor must
outlive the grant, and publication must join before destruction.

Publication patches a bounded prefix and uses a precomputed IEEE CRC shift
matrix to combine its checksum with the saved tail checksum. It performs no
payload copy, payload checksum scan or WAL encoding allocation. It enters the
same group-commit coordinator as ordinary appends, preserving the wire format,
LSN assignment and durability completion path. Preparation and abandonment spend
no LSN; each token allows one publication attempt. The HA and WAL buffers remain
separately owned and charged; this change does not consolidate them. Storage
owner ABI 100 gains additive prepare/publish/destroy entry points; native ABI
27 fences the updated runtime contract.

Regression coverage compares concatenated CRCs across empty, boundary and large
partitions, refuses each construction checkpoint and allocation, verifies
immutable ownership and single use, and mixes a prepared large entry with an
ordinary entry in one real backend transaction. Native publication succeeds
with the WAL encoding allocator denied while the ordinary large append fails.
The real compiled owner checks allocation cleanup, abandoned grants and
interleaved LSN assignment. The compiled client checks ignored original refusal,
returned-handle retirement and detachment from the original control after prep.
Both compiled boundary tests are included in the normal build target filters.

28 directly executed standard provider/client cases, with native Debug
steps 144/144 and all 5,120 inputs exactly current.

those filters and includes both. The compiled Primary fixture also gained its
existing controlled-read export, which the new payload readback requires. See `native-wal-prepaid-encoding-v3-verified.json` and its post-GC
receipt for exact input hashes and test evidence.

This funds encoding memory and payload CPU before local commit. Backend
transaction/LSM working memory, I/O admission and other completion dependencies

### Exact, controlled replay-envelope encoding

CJ2 replay records now have an allocation-free exact wire-size calculation that
checks list and key lengths against the format's u32 limits and checks aggregate
size arithmetic. Encoding acquires one exact output buffer before copying;
legacy geometric growth and its extra live backing allocations are removed.
Original controls are checked during size traversal, every 64 metadata entries,
at 4 KiB copy boundaries, after allocation and before returning the buffer.
An original refusal takes precedence over a later allocator failure, and any
partial buffer is freed. Both thin and materialized mutation replay encoders use
the same original control as prepared HA publication. Physical apply fences
retain their runnable admission; this adds bounded lifetime checks, not runnable
suspension while holding those fences. The runtime ABI remains 27 and CJ2 bytes
remain unchanged.

The new normal target `docstore-replay-encoding-test` includes three regressions:
all field masks and copy boundaries match the former encoder in an exactly sized
fixed buffer; every construction checkpoint and allocation failure unwinds; and
oversized wire lengths fail before allocation or key access. Existing replay,
transaction transform/full-text visibility, graph materialization, publication,
metadata and transaction HA/partial-ACK cases also run. Qualification passed
76 distinct functional cases and 99/99 native Debug build steps,
with all 5,120 source/schema inputs exactly current. The
current public archive matches 4,409 files and passes 25/25 independent
ReleaseSafe consumer checks. See `native-replay-exact-encoding-v1-verified.json` and its post-GC receipt.

This provides an authoritative size for an assembled immutable replay record.
PREPARE still needs a stable bound on its future artifact-key set, including
background artifact growth and graph endpoint notifications. Transaction replay
outboxes remain outside the batch-credit guarantee; adding fresh admission at
resolution would not fund an already globally committed obligation. Key-set
assembly, backend completion RAM/CPU/I/O bundles, whole-node policy, the remaining
physical resource graph and full original scheduler scope remain incomplete.
Full Linux qualification remains waived; Linux builds use pinned Nix glibc Zig.

### Physical artifact replay inventory (native ABI 28)

DocStore now maintains per-document physical derived-key counts and key bytes for
the families classified by artifact_footprint. Ordinary transactions, batches and
append writers coalesce the touched keys. Commit compares actual staged key
presence with committed presence through native metadata probes, then stages exact
counter deltas in the same physical transaction as the artifacts. Artifact values
are not copied to compute these facts. Counter metadata is staged after the bulk
append phase, avoiding a counter write that drains the append arena per artifact.
The shared native publication mutation gate serializes inventory/debt RMW across
namespace views and releases on commit or abort. Footprint control writes share
that gate; ignored allocation/storage failures poison inventory publication.
Missing deletes and supported bulk fallback retain their prior behavior.

A checksummed local marker binds the inventory generation to artifact-footprint
epochs. A certified empty root starts complete, where absent counters mean zero.
Existing roots start partial, where absent counters mean unknown. Older writers
and import invalidation advance footprint epochs without refreshing the marker,
invalidating the totals. Reinitialization uses a new generation so old counters
cannot revive. Reserved inventory facts cannot be overwritten by ordinary writes.
Clear preserves the local generation fence and retires quarantined old counters;
logical and portable staging imports exclude donor inventory metadata.

Reconciliation walks one document's physical keys without artifact values, in
pages of at most 128 keys or a 64 KiB key-byte target and a 2 ms time target.
The first key can exceed the byte target, up to the existing 1 MiB transfer-key
ceiling. Underlying physical opens/searches remain synchronous. Cursor copy and
checksum work check original controls every 4 KiB. Document revision, generation
and progress CAS fence publication. Same-document mutation restarts its scan;
unrelated documents retain progress. No cursor or read snapshot survives a page.
Native ABI 28 fences the updated capture layout; other owner/request/offer ABIs
retain their existing versions.

Seven new regressions cover coalescing and abandonment through all writer forms,
legacy page restart and unrelated-document progress, two-view gate contention,
ignored allocation failure, actual WAL reopen/old-writer/import epoch rejection,
clear/reuse, checksums, arithmetic, large cursors and owned-key allocation cleanup.
A late append Unsupported regression first reproduced a phantom key count. The
corrected observer compares actual committed/staged membership rather than the
requested operation, preserving both ignored rejection and successful fallback.
Existing logical graph snapshot restore and portable graph restore also run.
Qualification passed 85 distinct functional cases, including
28 direct provider/client cases, and 152/152 native Debug steps.
The corrected public archive matches 4,410 source files and passes 25/25
independent ReleaseSafe consumer checks. The first package export exposed an incorrect SPDX header on the new file; it
was corrected to Apache-2.0 before this final native and package qualification.
Every native source/schema input is exactly current, with no source exceptions. See
`native-artifact-replay-inventory-v2-verified.json` and its post-GC receipt.

These are facts about current physical keys, not a bound on every future
transaction effect. PREPARE replay credit and atomic background-credit adjustment
remain open. Full-sync resolution can generate provider-dependent artifacts;
prepared generated effects or a correct owned postdecision protocol is also
required. Catalog changes that alter possible effects need compatible pinning.
The minimum completion RAM/CPU/I/O bundle, full capture CPU accounting, whole-node
policy, remaining physical graph and original scheduler scope remain incomplete.
Full Linux qualification remains waived; Linux builds use pinned Nix glibc Zig.

### Distributed preparation and replay-funding dependency audit

The [transaction completion protocol](WORKLOAD_SCHEDULING.md#transaction-completion-before-the-commit-decision)
now records the source-verified dependency between generated effects and PREPARE
replay credit. The coordinator sends strong sync levels to followers after its
own durable commit, while PREPARE has no sync-level contract. Eligible generated
work currently runs during resolution; recovery uses weaker acknowledgement
levels. Current artifact inventory therefore cannot establish a complete bound
on those future effects.

The required next implementation is a versioned durable preparation contract and
canonical generated-effect representation, followed by predecision production
and reservation integration. The protocol preserves deferred graph/PDF work,
requires deterministic replicated application and restart semantics, and defines
atomic background-growth credit updates. This is a source audit and design
decision, not an implemented protocol or runtime qualification. Evidence is in
`native-transaction-preparation-protocol-audit-v1.json`; prior native and package
qualification remains attached to its existing source snapshots.

### Durable prepared generated-effect codec

`storage/db/prepared_transaction_effects.zig` now encodes all seven
PrecomputedGeneratedBatch families in a checksummed ATPE v1 frame. The contract
binds transaction ID, intent revision, intent digest, catalog digest, optional
schema version and deferred/synchronous preparation mode. Request-local text
roots and source accounting are omitted; schema and write-plan generations are
preserved. Binary keys, optional fields and float bits survive round trips.

The encoder measures exact frame size and bounded decode storage before its one
allocation. The decoder validates checksum, tags, lengths, identity and complete
consumption before allocating one backing buffer. Counts cannot allocate
unbounded descriptor arrays. Limits are 64 MiB encoded and 256 MiB decoded.
Owned decoded slices survive overwriting/freeing the input; the Decoded owner
releases the slab once, rather than using per-field effect cleanup. No control
borrow survives the call. Copies and hashes check original controls at 4 KiB
boundaries; structural traversal also checks them.

Four new regressions cover every effect family and a fixed wire fixture,
malformed/truncated records and identity changes, allocation failures, and
original-control rejection during copying, checksumming and decoding. The
normal target has a dedicated server/local test partition and selection audit;
an initial empty selection was rejected and the root was corrected. Final
native qualification passed 13 distinct cases, including existing prepare batch
credit and publication backlog regressions, and 79/79 build steps. All 5,123
native inputs match current source. The exported archive matches 4,411 public
source files and its independent ReleaseSafe consumer passed 25/25 compile
steps. These consumer steps do not exercise transaction recovery or PREPARE.
See `native-prepared-transaction-effects-v5-verified.json`.

This implements the representation only. PREPARE does not persist or negotiate
it, and resolution does not consume it. Next connect it atomically to intent
revision/cleanup and peer negotiation, then run eligible producers before the
commit decision, and finally fund replay and background growth. The decoded
slab owner must be retained through materialization; handing its slices to
existing per-field deinit would violate ownership. Resource grants, actual
restart/abort lifecycle, minimum completion bundles, remaining write families,
whole-node policy and the full scheduler/default-policy scope remain open.
No runtime ABI changed. Full Linux qualification remains waived.

### Durable transaction effect sealing and retention admission

TxnManager now seals an immutable ATPE frame against its actual prepared intent

The durable schema lease supplies the schema version; the DB owner supplies the
catalog digest and preparation mode under existing apply ownership. Catalog
identity must include table/shard identity and retained catalog generations before

Frame storage joins the existing DocStore publication backlog: exact frame/key
bytes and one record are admitted and committed with their size/aggregate facts.
Refusal leaves the prior prepare mutable. An identical lost-reply retry preserves
the accepted frame, revision and credit; a conflicting result cannot replace it.
Accepted seals freeze further incremental intent writes. Raw backend bypass is
outside this accounting guarantee; no new request path invokes sealing yet.

Loading verifies current intent/schema binding and owns one decoded slab.
Plan-aware low-level resolution checks the accepted fingerprint and revision,
then retires the plan and retention credit atomically with the supplied effects
and intent cleanup. The trusted materializer still supplies every effect family;
this API does not perform inference or reconstruct every index/coverage effect.
Legacy commit resolution refuses a sealed plan. Abort retires even corrupt opaque
plans. Terminal conflicts keep their established error and trace behavior.
Committed resolved records with leftover plans remain fenced for repair and GC;
terminal abort can retire an orphan plan. HA batch credits remain independent.

The intentional pressured-shutdown fixture now declares exactly one expected

### Authoritative primary-key floor at the replay seal

The funded seal now retains the exact intent snapshot used for its digest while

intents use the same classification as transaction application and do not acquire

`deriveWithPrimaryKeys` tracks only borrowed authoritative keys and marks lanes

not actual replay notifications or primary application semantics. Input and
accepted-effect decode owners retire before the publication writer opens; the
plan retains only its owned root prefixes and scalar wire totals.

### Retained preparation dependencies and transform ABA protection

preparation, existing extraction-plan and relational-index views, and a clone of

apply/publication fence at capture and immediately before local publication.

physical/native owner after local commit, before remote or visibility waits;

changes. The revision probe retires before timestamp checks; validation no

### Durable read observations and exact cursor bounds (2026-10-21)

prepared_read_set.Durable now encodes/decodes sealed observations as ATRO v1.
The envelope binds the full effect contract (transaction, intent revision and
digest, catalog, optional schema and mode), participant/topology/route binding,
accepted effect-frame digest and physical namespace. Point keys include value
fingerprints or absence. Cursor programs retain physical/logical payload mode,
explicit operation tags, owned arguments and key/value fingerprints including
null stopping rows. Decode retains no frame, source, cursor or caller control.

The little-endian format has a 250-byte header and SHA256 trailer; the empty
envelope is 282 bytes, frozen against an independently packed golden digest.
Frame size is capped at 64 MiB; the combined point/cursor/operation count is
capped at 65,536. Count and minimum-body checks precede allocations, including
32-bit overflow checks. Original rejection causes survive checksum/copy and
allocation failures; partially decoded points/cursors/arguments unwind exactly.
Malformed tags, booleans, lengths, reserved fields, trailing/truncated records
and wrong contracts are rejected. This also fixes capture/replay aliasing of
an empty upper bound with clearing a bound: they now use distinct operations.
Native55/storage-owner113 reject prior native observations; public failure IDs,
API59, failure67, descriptorv29 and existing prepared-reader versions are unchanged.

Four codec regressions cover both payload modes, every cursor operation, binary
keys, source/frame retirement, all-byte corruption/truncation, authenticated
structural truncation, all 12 binding components, excessive counts, exhaustive
allocator failures and each original NotFound/OOM/deadline checkpoint. A native
DB fixture persists bytes, retires the original capture/handle, reopens, decodes
and detects point/absence changes and range phantoms. Final evidence is

### Owned semantic read footprints (2026-10-21)

prepared_read_set.Footprint.compile now replays/validates captured point reads
and cursor programs on one immutable primary snapshot, then owns normalized
key intervals for every observed point, gap and stopping boundary. Inclusive
and exclusive endpoints, binary/NUL keys, unbounded ends, forward/reverse
movement, empty/cleared upper bounds and exhausted cursor state are explicit.
Logical observations resolve payloads through the same snapshot's point reader;
physical observations fingerprint raw cursor values. No source key buffer,
cursor, frame, payload session or control pointer survives compilation.

The compiler checks at most 65,536 point/cursor/operation descriptors and copies
at most 64 MiB of keys; caller allocator ownership and read/payload budgets stay
separate. It rejects unsealed/poisoned/active programs, malformed operation
shapes, unordered or non-snapshot readers and changed results. Controlled
chunk comparisons, bottom-up merge sort and binary conflict lookup propagate
every original rejection rather than swallowing cancellation in a comparator.
Empty input needs no allocation or read. Allocation failure unwinds the arena.

Backend semantic_cursor_bounds defaults false. LSM snapshot cursors explicitly
guarantee exclusive bounds in both directions, unchanged position on bound
updates and stable null next/prev after exhaustion. Unknown adapters use
conservative footprints; an optimization hint is never assumed to fence a
read. Native57/storage-owner115 fence the added capability. Reader14, ATROv1,
API59/failure67/descriptorv29 and public error IDs remain unchanged.

DBCore.compilePreparedReadFootprint loads the accepted bound observation seal
for its actual namespace and supplied participant binding, validates reads and

apply/catalog/route ownership and must revalidate the receipt at later admission.

Capture acquires the shared publication gate before reading the original count
and each touched guard's original membership. It owns copied metadata keys,
not borrowed backend values or caller authority pointers. Scope changes and
other owners' framed guard keys are rejected and poison the writer. Final
validation requires admission to leave guards present, resolution to remove
existing guards, and the final count to equal the original count plus the exact
membership delta. Empty values and exact key framing are mandatory. Count
changes refresh the reader-presence fast path, so a guard installed before a
later data mutation cannot be skipped. The absent-reader path still makes one
count lookup; metadata bookkeeping is allocated only when metadata is touched.

admission, or a terminal record with known completed intent resolution for

batch and resolution scope at the final decision/resource batch. A backend
claiming `owned_read_guard_mutations` must provide the native scope operation;

### Assembly-derived replay reservation (2026-10-21)

DocStore transactions, batches and batch adapters can reserve replay retention
from the owning assembler's detached physical batch. The writer independently
loads the exact accepted frame, checks its expected contract and fingerprint,
and reconstructs the complete stored-intent floor with schema, birth/revision,
digest and lock checks. The grant covers both views: it unions their distinct
physical document roots and takes the maximum count and key bytes in each
canonical replay lane. Auxiliary group/generated roots enter the reservation;
logical no-ops cannot remove the original primary floor. Overlapping lanes and
roots are not added twice.

validation. Reservation failure poisons the writer, including malformed replay,
changed inputs and original-control rejection. Retrying an identical reservation
is idempotent. This stages only credit and claims; detached document postimages
are not published. The native owner must still validate the candidate's live
dependencies under apply before opening this reservation writer.

bundle. Replay sequence relocation and progress-safe counters, backend-generated
commit metadata, durable read guards, live route/lifetime ownership, derived-log

### Commit-boundary replay sequence claims

The shared normal mutation path now assembles against the observed next replay
sequence under apply and claims that exact value at the final precommit boundary.
Pure assembly, backlog admission, publication-envelope preparation, preparation
admission checks and retained dependency validation precede the claim. A rejected
preparation therefore does not advance the process-local clock or invalidate a
held candidate merely by consuming a sequence number.

The storage owner conditionally advances the clock with a compare-and-exchange.
A competing reservation rejects the candidate rather than publishing metadata
and replay bytes at different sequences. The existing preparation retry wrapper
can rebuild it; repeated conflicts stop after its three-attempt budget. Ordinary mutations and accepted
transaction resolution share this boundary. Semantic no-op replay elision keeps
its existing behavior; preparation-only assembly still reserves nothing.
Only a successful atomic writer advances the durable replay cut. Writer admission
or staging failure, or uncertain commit after the claim, can retain an unused
process-local number;
such reservations are never rolled back or handed to another live candidate.

### Owned commit-memory state and completion retirement

Prepared assemblies now own scalar visibility-summary and table-catalog
postimages. Capture checks the native producer's values against their last

checks those witnesses before commit. Replay refresh updates the summary's native

generations and independent catalog generations remain unchanged. The state
contains no borrowed request buffers or controls.

After a successful primary outcome and retirement of preparation readers, the
normal mutation path adopts these facts and clears obsolete visibility caches
before fallible replication publication or committed-effects observers. A failed
completion can therefore leave the caller with an error while queries and later
writes still use the committed cardinality and visibility state. Range and reader
floor adoption retain their existing position relative to preparation retirement.

The same boundary transfers the admitted derived-backlog reservation to the
executor's committed tracker. Completion failure can no longer cancel the quota
for replay bytes already committed. The transfer uses the capacity reserved before
commit and performs no allocation. A degraded producer still reaches the hard
backlog limit even if every accepted write's observer fails.

A synchronous per-invocation marker records an observed primary commit or terminal
resolution. It propagates to an enclosing synchronous caller but is never retained
by an assembly. The preparation retry wrapper preserves a completion error's
identity while refusing to rerun an accepted batch, including when the error has a
preparation-conflict name. Precommit conflicts retain their existing retry bound.

it does not change public error or durability protocols.

### Retained derived-log credits

A retained assembly now admits its actual replay bytes against the same node-wide
derived-backlog quota as an ordinary source commit. It owns that credit until
cancellation or transfer after a successful primary outcome. The handoff occurs
only after dependency and sequence validation; every earlier failure cancels the
local credit. No storage mutation, sequence claim, provider invocation or wait is
needed to retain or release it. Refresh keeps the same fixed-width replay payload
and does not reacquire quota. A configured quota therefore bounds concurrently
retained candidates that append replay as well as committed replay debt. Candidates
without replay owe no derived-log credit and still need the separate preparation
and recovery memory budget.

Tracker admissions now reserve independent future entry slots. Recovery tracking
preserves those slots while appending records; a later primary commit can transfer
any retained credit without allocation. The runtime serializes admission, tracking
and transfer. Cancellation outside its lock only decrements an atomic slot count
and returns the memory reservation. Teardown requires all outstanding admissions
to have retired. Empty admissions without a resource manager retain the existing
behavior and are not evidence of a funded executable recovery bundle.

layout. Durable formats, reader floors and default scheduling activation remain

### Caller-owned scheduled candidate drain

`DB.drainPreparedAssembliesWithAdmission` adds an explicit closing phase for a
caller that still owns runnable capacity needed by an active candidate. It
requires the original admission port's finite deadline and checked execution-wait
boundary. The phase fences candidate operations, returns unused replay credits
and live dependency pins, and leaves physical DB/worker teardown to its existing
closing owner. Callers must fence general DB admission and keep the DB and output
allocators alive until their mandatory cleanup completes.

The registry now separates closing intent, its current finisher and a detached
pending list. `tryClose` never waits for an active guard or competing retirement
callback. The controlled phase lends runnable ownership only during those waits,
polls the original lifetime while parked, and always rejoins the original wait
boundary before another retirement attempt. It performs callback cleanup under
running ownership, never around a whole backend/close call, and creates no new
execution owner, deadline or resource reservation.

Begin, parked-lifetime and reentry failures leave the registry fenced and
resumable. Completed callbacks stay completed; the pending list continues to own
remaining references, including a tail concurrently retired by its caller. An
original cleanup owner can retry without repeating callbacks or losing the DB
obligation. Missing execution-wait or finite-deadline metadata refuses controlled
retirement before callbacks. Compatibility close continues to serve quiesced
callers whose ownership cannot prevent the drained work from executing.

Durable formats, reader floors and default activation are unchanged. This is the
retained-candidate drain phase; lending/ownership for other worker/cache/IO joins,

providers remain disabled. Full Linux qualification remains waived; Linux uses

### Cooperative candidate retirement turns

Scheduled candidate draining now checkpoints between individual retirements.
Previously `tryClose` detached and marked the entire registry, then ran every
ready callback under one checkpoint. A large ready registry could therefore
skip scheduler fairness and original-lifetime checks for its whole teardown.
The controlled path now distinguishes completed, progressed and waiting states.
Progress returns directly to the original checkpoint; only active guards or a
competing callback use the original execution-wait boundary.

Each turn detaches one node in constant time and retains that registry reference
until retirement completes. The rest remain linked, allowing concurrent caller
cancellation to detach its own node without a whole-list scan. The finisher and
registry lock are released before the next checkpoint. Original rejection or
deadline expiry after a retired prefix leaves the tail fenced and owned for the
original mandatory cleanup path. Completed callbacks do not repeat. A concurrent
linked cancellation remains counted as active until its callback joins, so
physical teardown cannot pass it. Compatibility close still eagerly retires
ready nodes for quiesced callers.

Registration metadata now uses the owner's independent allocator. A detached
registry reference can survive the caller's candidate destruction; allocating
that node from the candidate allocator let a caller arena disappear before a
resumable finisher read/unreferenced the node. Payload retirement still completes
before caller destruction returns. Only stable metadata survives it, and the
last node reference releases the owner. Independent metadata accounting and
funding remain part of the broader resource-parent work.

semantics. Durable formats, reader floors and default activation are unchanged.
This bounds registry work and callback count per checkpoint. Individual callback

the remaining scheduler design remain open. Strong required providers remain

### Exclusive dense finalization preparation

Controlled finish preparation now claims the exact session before acquiring
catalog/apply guards. Competing finalizers wait with their original finite
control; competing token transfers and new batch-admission borrows cannot take
ownership from the preparing callback. Existing independently retained snapshot
leases remain valid. A competing abort reports a retryable rejection instead of
silently reporting that it removed a session still owned by preparation.

cannot invalidate a preparation claim. Releasing an unconsumed claim uses one
atomic store, requires no registry lock, and leaves its original token, native
capture, snapshot lease and cleanup reservation in the registry. Taking through
a claim uses a nonblocking registry attempt; a busy registry causes apply guards
to be dropped before another bounded wait. Transfer releases the stable metadata
and moves the existing physical ownership without allocating. Capture funding
includes the stable metadata allocation. Native ABI 87 and storage-owner ABI 145
fence the registry layout change.

it does not activate reserved CPU or move durable callback work onto it yet.

and CPU bounds, other retirement paths, and the wider design gates remain open.

may still run.

### Controlled detached-index pin retirement

Physical index destruction waits for detached graph-worker snapshots that borrow
inline graph-index entries. DB close preflight now drains these pins after derived
finalization and before durable backend admission closes. Accepted pin users can
still submit their dependent backend work, and they can acquire the CPU needed to
retire while the original closer is parked. The same DB/index generation remains
alive after a rejected handoff, lifetime or reentry check for exact retry.

A permanent snapshot-admission flag is separate from restartable graph topology
retirement and artifact-rebuild admission. New snapshot capture checks it before
and under the catalog shared lock. Controlled close publishes the flag and takes
an admitted exclusive catalog barrier, ensuring an earlier installer has published
its pin before drainage observes the counter. That barrier is released before
waiting for existing workers. Compatibility physical destruction uses the same
catalog barrier under its existing quiesced-cleanup ownership.

Readiness while CPU is parked observes only the atomic pin counter. After reentry,
close acquires the pin-retirement mutex with the original finite control and
rechecks zero. The last releaser decrements under that mutex before notifying and
unlocking; counter zero alone cannot authorize destroying its still-used metadata.
No original admission port is retained in the manager, snapshot or background job.
Native ABI 97 and storage-owner ABI 157 fence the new index-manager layout and
close-preflight dependency contract.

Final status persistence, physical index/backend I/O and LSM generation-reader
retirement still need controlled close contracts. Callback CPU/I/O adoption,
remaining resource charging and broader original design requirements also remain
unfinished. This change drains detached graph snapshot pins, not all physical
index or storage ownership. The full goal remains active; full GNU/Linux
qualification remains waived and Linux builds require pinned Nix/glibc Zig.

### Owning physical durability operations

Native storage exposes owning file-content and parent-directory sync operations.
Preparation, bounded pathname copying, descriptor admission and dispatch happen
under the original finite caller control. Physical callbacks only open, sync and
close the prepared path. They do not decode WAL metadata, flush memtables, compact,
construct manifests or borrow the caller's admission port. Worker refusal returns
ConcurrencyUnavailable without a synchronous fallback.

An accepted operation retains native storage state, its executor/allocator and
one process-shared descriptor permit until explicit deinit. That permit bounds
retained operation metadata as well as in-flight descriptor use, including owners
whose controlled wait was rejected. A failed handoff, lifetime or reentry leaves
the same operation available for retry; retry observes one physical result and
does not issue another sync. Atomic completion is observed while CPU is parked;
physical join and result publication follow successful original reentry. Quiesced
deinit performs the mandatory physical join and releases the permit last, outside
the callback that owns the retained executor.

Descriptor preparation supplies a synchronous adapter for finite wait/retry, so
callers need no backend-specific progress callback. The existing descriptor FIFO
now performs a lifetime-only check under its admission mutex. Yielding checkpoints
and wait/reentry happen after releasing the guard; a caller checkpoint cannot
retain the descriptor mutex while its CPU is parked. Missing owning providers,
missing finite authority and unsupported native descriptor ledgers fail closed.
POSIX native storage and its retained-lease views implement the new capability;
legacy synchronous and logical-memory providers remain separate.

The operation retains executor and descriptor ownership, not a logical filesystem
publication generation. Its coordinator must retain WAL/file publication ownership
through physical completion, including rejected waits. Native ABI 98 and
storage-owner ABI 158 fence the optional provider extensions and operation layout.
This is the physical durability layer. Final DB close does not yet use it for WAL
metadata preparation, ordered WAL sync, final status persistence or backend flush/
retirement. Those phases need owning resumable coordinators; wrapping an entire
backend flush as an I/O wait would run backend CPU without execution capacity.
The full goal stays active. Full GNU/Linux qualification remains waived; Linux
builds require pinned Nix/glibc Zig.

### Owning bounded durability metadata reads

Storage now exposes an owning control-file read with a hard 4 KiB limit. Caller
CPU validates the requested limit and prepares bounded path/output storage plus
shared descriptor admission before dispatch. The physical task opens one file,
observes its size and reads at most the admitted bytes through that same handle.
Oversized files return the observed size and no payload; no unbounded file is
hydrated. WAL checksum/format validation remains on admitted caller CPU.

The operation retains its result buffer, native storage state, executor and
shared descriptor permit across rejected handoff, lifetime and reentry. Successful
original reentry precedes physical join and result observation. Returned bytes
borrow from that operation until explicit deinit; repeated waits observe the same
bytes rather than rereading a replaced CURRENT path. Missing owning providers,
invalid size budgets, allocation rejection and executor saturation fail closed.
The shared native physical-operation implementation now supplies file/parent sync
and control-file reads while preserving their distinct result contracts. Native
ABI 99 and storage-owner ABI 159 fence the provider/result extensions.

This provides the physical metadata stage required by controlled WAL sync. It
is not yet a WAL coordinator or final-close adoption. A coordinator must retain
WAL publication ownership and arrange minimum reusable completion resources
before taking that lock. Holding a publication lock and then waiting for a new
descriptor/worker grant can create a dependency cycle. Compound acquisition must
release tentative resources before waiting when publication cannot be acquired;
accepted physical stages retain all their ownership through failure and retry.
Further work includes that completion-resource/coordinator contract, ordered
CURRENT/segment durability, final status/backend persistence and physical reader/
I/O retirement. The full goal remains active. Full GNU/Linux qualification remains
waived; Linux builds require pinned Nix/glibc Zig.

### Reusable physical durability completion resources

Storage can now prepare one owning durability grant before acquiring publication.
Its nonblocking descriptor try honors queued FD waiters and refuses busy admission
metadata without holding a partial grant. Preparation retains the native state,
reserves one shared descriptor, allocates fixed pathname/control-file storage and
admits one mailbox worker. Missing providers or execution-wait/deadline authority,
allocation rejection and dispatch refusal fail closed; there is no raw-I/O fallback.
Native ABI 100 and storage-owner ABI 160 fence the added provider and grant vtables.

A serialized phase copies its bounded input on caller CPU and reuses that worker
and descriptor for a control-file read, file sync or parent-directory sync. The
worker performs only physical I/O and bounded mailbox bookkeeping. It retains no
original admission port. Atomic completion publishes results before reuse; a
rejected wait retains the exact phase and its bytes/error until explicit retirement.
A second phase cannot overwrite a live result. Quiesced grant retirement finishes
accepted work before stopping/joining the worker, then releases state/descriptor
ownership last, outside that worker.

The resource-ordering requirement remains explicit: a coordinator must try WAL
publication after preparing an idle grant, and drop the tentative grant before
waiting if publication is busy. Otherwise a legacy publication holder waiting for
an FD could deadlock against a closer retaining FDs while waiting for publication.
This change supplies the reusable completion resources; it does not yet acquire
WAL publication or replace default DB final persistence with controlled phases.
The next implementation is compound acquisition and an owning, ordered CURRENT
read/validation, segment-sync and CURRENT-sync coordinator. Final status writes,
backend flush, reader/I/O retirement and provider adoption remain open. The full
goal is active; full GNU/Linux qualification remains waived, and Linux builds
require the pinned Nix/glibc toolchain.

### Owning WAL durability cut and compound publication acquisition

The local LSM backend can now prepare bounded paths and try to acquire a reusable
completion grant together with its existing process/native WAL publication guards.
A busy publication guard drops the idle grant before the original execution waits.
FD pressure likewise leaves no publication ownership. This path requires already
prepared lock files/root metadata and never opens them as an implicit acquisition
fallback. Waiting uses the supplied finite execution authority without extending
its deadline. No backend mutex survives acquisition or physical waits.

`CurrentStateSync(Publication)` owns the grant, publication and one pending phase.
It reads actual CURRENT (`wal/index`) through one bounded physical operation,
validates its exact size, format, checksum and nonzero segment on admitted CPU,
then syncs the named segment before CURRENT. It uses prepared descriptor/worker/
buffer resources for every physical phase. A missing referenced segment is an
error rather than permission to create an empty replacement. Corrupt or oversized
metadata cannot proceed to either barrier. A genuinely absent CURRENT returns an
empty sync result. An original FileNotFound rejection is identified by its
rejection trace and preserves the pending read and publication instead.

Rejected handoff, lifetime or reentry leaves the accepted phase available for
retry without replaying completed I/O. Successful admitted observation advances
only that phase; completed results and terminal physical/validation failures are
stable. Publication releases after admitted terminal observation. Mandatory
quiesced destruction joins the currently accepted physical operation before
releasing publication, then retires the idle worker and descriptor. It performs
no new decoding or unissued sync stages during destruction.

The backend entry points are explicitly for a quiesced, retained backend with a
single owning sync/close continuation. Its caller must fence writers/maintenance,
retain the backend until retirement and ensure cleanup reentry can progress while
legacy publication acquirers hold ordinary capacity. The real-backend tests use
an independently reserved, finite protected cleanup root. These are internal
coordinator APIs; existing native payload layouts/vtables remain ABI 100 and
storage-owner ABI 160. Default final-close adoption remains open.

CURRENT, size/checksum/zero-segment corruption, a missing referenced segment and
successful idempotent completion. Real-backend cases leave only one descriptor
available and prove the publication holder can acquire it when cleanup parks;
acquisition rejection owns no tentative grant. Accepted read rejection retains
both actual guards, and missing prepared metadata fails without an implicit open.
A real read-only peer remains blocked during mandatory join of a paused read and
acquires both publication guards after retirement, while backend metadata remains
unlocked throughout.

cursor and an optional text snapshot pin. Original admission rejection preserves
completed rows and partial progress; a retry resumes the same capture. One
logical finisher owns progress while competing finishers wait through their own
finite original execution authority. No admission callback borrow is retained.

Text capture pins serving metadata without triggering residency maintenance and
checkpoints between segments. Dense and graph counters use admitted metadata
guards. Sparse counter fallback reads use an admitted probe rather than the
legacy raw stats read. Keys copy in bounded CPU quanta. Final physical close
consumes the captured bytes and releases their storage and snapshot pins before
index/runtime teardown. Legacy close without completed controlled capture still
uses its previous collection path. Native ABI 101 and storage-owner ABI 161
account for the new DB-owned state.

### Prepared owning physical append resources

Final status commit cannot safely park the entire legacy batch commit: that
callback combines CPU preparation/publication with physical WAL operations.
The durability provider now offers a prepared append grant as a prerequisite to
separating those phases. Preparation freezes encoded input in the retained native
state's allocator with checkpoints between 16 KiB copy quanta, reserves one
shared descriptor and starts one reusable mailbox worker before publication is
acquired. Error or descriptor refusal transfers no grant and performs no write.
Partial-copy, allocation and dispatch failures roll back buffers and capacity.

An accepted append owns its immutable bytes, descriptor and worker through
handoff, lifetime and reentry rejection, including destruction of the storage
owner and lease. Retrying the wait observes the same accepted operation; it does
not append again. Append, control read, content sync and parent sync share the
same serial grant. Physical execution adds no allocator/worker/descriptor
admission. Append does not imply fsync, directory creation or permission to
fabricate a missing referenced segment. Creation is explicit. A physical failure
can leave a partial tail; the future WAL publication owner must recover that
ambiguity rather than resubmit the record. Mandatory retirement joins accepted
work before freeing its frozen bytes and releasing the descriptor/runtime.

Native ABI 102 and storage-owner ABI 162 cover the additional storage/resource
callbacks. Providers without this capability fail closed. Default close has not
yet adopted the append primitive: the next owning WAL append coordinator must
retain publication, decode actual CURRENT and plan segment transitions on CPU,
append prepared bytes, publish mutable state exactly once, and order its final
barriers before releasing publication. Status commit and final backend flush
must then compose with it without later writes or duplicate legacy sync.

goal remains active; full GNU qualification remains waived.

### Owning canonical WAL append and publication

`prepareStateRecordWithAdmission` encodes the existing canonical state-record
format on caller CPU, with checked sizes and checkpoints between entries, 16 KiB
copy quanta and streaming checksum quanta. Preparation rejection frees its
speculative bytes before any publication acquisition or physical dispatch. The
backend validates framing, checksum, entry lengths and count on admitted CPU
before preparing an append grant.

`CurrentStateAppend(Publication)` owns actual CURRENT observation, bootstrap,
segment-size observation, rotation, bounded metadata replacement, one frozen
append and its ordered durability barriers. CURRENT's advisory size never
substitutes for the actual segment size. An existing CURRENT cannot fabricate a
missing referenced segment. Orphan checkpoints, nonempty unclaimed segments,
corrupt metadata and segment-number overflow fail closed. Bootstrap creates only
the WAL child of an existing root, syncs its namespace, atomically persists
CURRENT and the initial checkpoint, appends once and syncs the new segment and
its directory. Rotation persists the new CURRENT and preserves prior retention
history; steady append performs no redundant metadata replacement.

The reusable durability grant now supports small atomic metadata replacement
and single-directory creation, with fixed buffers and no new allocation,
descriptor admission or dispatch during physical phases. Replacement owns a
reserved sibling temporary under exclusive filesystem publication, exclusively
creates it after removing a stale reserved temporary, syncs and closes it,
renames it and syncs its parent. Native ABI 103 and storage-owner ABI 163 cover
the additional callbacks. Unsupported providers fail closed.

Metadata replacement fences the inode cache on admitted caller CPU before
submission and after physical observation, including ambiguous physical failure.
The fence marks entries without closing descriptors or freeing memory under the
cache guard; existing read pins remain valid. The metadata bucket walk is
bounded by the shared descriptor ceiling. Rejection while acquiring a cache
guard retains the completed physical operation and its pending fence. Mandatory
quiesced retirement applies any outstanding fence before publication release.
The worker performs no cache bookkeeping. A warmed-CURRENT rotation regression
and a held-cache-guard regression prove fresh inode lookup alongside retained
old readers.

Successful WAL I/O retains publication until `publishWithAdmission` adopts an
already-prepared mutable successor through a bounded infallible CPU callback.
No reentry checkpoint splits that adoption from its once-only receipt and
publication release. Original handoff/lifetime/reentry rejection retains each
accepted phase without replay. A fatal physical failure, possible partial tail,
or quiesced destruction after accepted mutation but before adoption requests
recovery before releasing publication. Destruction joins accepted work only;
it never issues unstarted barriers or adopts caller state.

The backend compound acquisition prepares frozen record/worker/descriptor
resources before trying its real process/native WAL guards. Busy acquisition
drops every tentative resource before the original waits; the caller still owns
its prepared publication payload until the initial read is accepted. Successful
adoption updates fixed WAL counters/ranges and invalidates retention caches.
Abandoned possible writes poison backend mutation until recovery. No backend
mutex spans physical waits. The caller must already fence serving, writers and
maintenance and retain the backend and prepared publication through retirement.

retains consumer publication across rejected adoption. Final source/log hashes
match; v1/v2 retain the intermediate fixture and cache-fence corrections.

Default DB close adoption remains unfinished. Its final status commit must own
bounded mutable/capture preparation and credits, use this publication protocol,
then compose with admitted backend flush and physical retirement. A final
barrier cannot precede later writes or be followed by duplicate legacy sync.
Equivalent Lite/object provider adoption also remains open. The complete goal
remains active; full GNU qualification remains waived and Linux builds require
the pinned Nix/glibc toolchain.

### Owning bounded mutable successor preparation

`ActiveMemTable.PublicationPreparation` moves immutable input and retains the
quiesced live root in constant time. Its allocation-free memory planning keeps
a row cursor and checked byte totals, so the caller can reserve construction
credit before successor allocation. The bound covers additional packed entries,
copy-on-write nodes, the node-pointer pool and its account; input residency and
encoded/frozen WAL bytes remain separate obligations.

Preparation retains completed rows, partial packed byte copies, node reservations
and comparison offsets across original admission rejection. Namespace/key/value
copies and namespace/key comparisons checkpoint in 16 KiB quanta. Node reservation
checks the original before each allocation and retains its partial pool on OOM.
The input and speculative successor stay owned without retaining an admission
borrow. The live root, its pool and existing reader snapshots remain unchanged.

Rank search finishes before tree mutation. A new prepaid AVL insertion uses only
child counts to insert or replace at that exact rank, avoiding unbounded key
comparison or a fallible checkpoint inside a partly changed shared path. The
edit and eventual publication swap are infallible, allocation-free and bounded
by AVL height. The caller must exclude intervening writers and handle backend
snapshot fencing and memory-credit adoption separately.

After publication the preparation owner retains the previous root. Before or
after publication, admitted retirement uses the existing allocation-free tree
and state reclamation continuations in 64-credit slices, including arena-backed
input. Rejected retirement keeps ownership and resumes from the same cursor.
Mandatory quiesced destruction drains the same owned continuations. Canonical
ordered-writer invariants exclude legacy flat/arena mutable generations from
this tree publication protocol until normalized.

The real backend WAL append regression now builds its successor with this owner,
encodes its retained input, publishes through the owning WAL coordinator and
retires through original CPU admission. Final receipt
`mutable-publication-preparation-v2` passes all 65 build steps, all 29 named
physical/WAL cases, all 16 independently compiled archive cases and 45/1/8
identity cases without skips, failures or leaks. The three new cases inject
each original failure at every planning/preparation checkpoint, fail every
preparation allocation, verify allocation-free adoption and pinned-reader
isolation, and abandon partial arena-backed and empty generations. Source and
log hashes match all 5,541 final inputs. The v1 receipt qualifies the first two
matrices before the added abandonment case.

Default DB close still uses ordinary status batch commit. The next integration
must own captured input/construction credit, adopt actual retained memory into
backend accounting, reserve manifest debt, fence mutable snapshots and compose
the prepared successor with owning WAL append. Admitted final backend flush,
retirement and equivalent Lite/object provider adoption remain open. This
preparation owner does not enable the complete default pooling gate; the full
goal remains active and full GNU qualification remains waived.

### Mutable publication construction credit and retained accounting

`Backend.QuiescedMutablePublication` now owns the successor's construction
credit, preparation and accounting through publication or abandonment. The
backend and its usage identity must stay stable and quiesced throughout this
owner. Input uses the backend allocator and has its own residency credit;
encoded and frozen WAL bytes also remain separate obligations.

Preparation first reserves observer metadata under original admission, including
an empty backend's zero-valued usage identity. It then reserves construction
credit against the checked successor bound before any successor allocation.
The manager-owned construction cleanup slot remains owned across preparation,
OOM, rejected adoption and WAL work. Adoption transfers only prepaid actual
growth into the backend's retained observer; it cannot silently admit excess
growth. The observer and reservation metadata are already present, so adoption
requires no new allocator capacity. Neither child nor parent ledger contention
retains Backend.mu or replaces the original caller's wait authority.

Actual successor growth is measured from its allocation account and node-pointer
pool. The owner retains that account until physical retirement finishes, avoiding
a full backend observer scan at the WAL boundary. Publication performs only the
prepared swap, with no ledger access, snapshot destruction or allocation. Cached
mutable snapshots must already be detached before creating the owner; debug
guards check that precondition at construction and publication.

Admitted retirement keeps released physical bytes charged until the child and
parent ledgers accept reconciliation. A speculative account header is physically
freed before its capacity is released, and the saved target survives rejected
ledger retries. Unused construction credit retires into the existing finite
manager-owned cleanup protocol. Published allocations remain charged in the
backend observer. Mandatory quiesced destruction follows the same ownership
ordering after the owning WAL operation joins.

Preparation reuses packed input only when it already belongs to the backend's
account. Unaccounted input is copied, preserving independent producer pins and
their construction credit through consumer abandonment. The ordered-tree bound
now includes ArrayList's actual cache-line minimum and vector relocation peak;
the former two-pointer-per-node estimate undercounted small pools on this host.

The real backend WAL regression now uses the credit-owning publication with a
resource manager for successful adoption, abandoned publication and actual
partial-append failure. Final receipt `mutable-publication-credit-v5` passes all
68 build steps, 31 physical/WAL cases, 32 storage-read cases, 16 independently
compiled archive cases and 45/1/8 identity cases without skips, failures or
leaks. Tests deny slice and parent capacity before data allocation, reject all
three original errors with the child ledger held before adoption and the parent
held after physical retirement, adopt with both allocators exhausted, and retain
producer data across partial new-account retirement. Exact retained usage matches
the backend's independent full estimate. Source/log hashes match all 5,541
inputs. Earlier receipts preserve the private-helper correction, detected bound
underestimate and fresh-fixture baseline correction; v4 passes before the final
snapshot guards and parent-contention coverage.

Default close adoption remains open. Before this delta owner is used there,
controlled close must detach snapshots and reconcile existing backend usage on
bounded admitted CPU. A fresh backend's cleanup queue is an example of existing
metadata that must be included in that baseline. Captured input and both WAL
representations still need their owning credits, alongside manifest debt and
the final status/WAL state machine. Admitted final backend flush/retirement and
Lite/object provider adoption remain unfinished. No complete default pooling
gate is enabled; the full goal remains active and full GNU qualification remains
waived.

### Default close snapshot fencing and bounded accounting preflight

Default controlled LSM close now retains a `QuiescedClosePreflight` in the final
status program. It runs after status capture and after producer, cache and durable
dependency drains, serialized by the program's logical finisher. Status capture
can still borrow primary read epochs, so the final snapshot fence follows it.

Preflight waits for all backend reader pins and the cached snapshot's own readers
under the original finite execution boundary. Backend.mu is released before any
wait. Once readers finish, a fixed metadata transition clears the cached snapshot,
removes its reader-reference registration and transfers its already-owned State
header to the backend's existing retirement queue. No payload destruction,
allocation, filesystem operation or new background job occurs during detachment.
Repeated calls never detach or queue a generation twice. The generation stays
reachable by both legacy accounting and eventual admitted physical retirement.

The owning accounting cursor covers the same retained components as the full
backend observer, including shared mutable roots, run/directory metadata, pending
and retired job lists, immutable generations, sparse bulk-account registries and
queued memory retirement. Fixed root/account aggregates are constant work;
variable lists advance one node per checkpoint. Flat rows, arena blocks and sparse
hash-table slots use at most 64 credits per CPU slice. Sparse iteration only calls
the standard iterator at an occupied slot, preventing its internal empty-slot
walk from bypassing admission. Frozen arenas reuse their recorded charge;
unfrozen arenas use one-node views of the pinned allocator's capacity calculation.

Progress retains its pass, visitation cursors and accumulated total across original
failure without borrowing a caller scope. The caller must fence mutation and
competing accounting observations for the unfinished pass; default close already
owns the serving and producer fences. Final ledger reconciliation uses original
admission and can admit observer metadata for previously unobserved existing
allocations. Rejection, including metadata OOM, retains the computed total and
backend-owned payloads for retry. This establishes the baseline required by the
credit-owning mutable publication without a raw whole-backend walk.

Native ABI 104 and storage-owner ABI 164 cover the new DB-owned continuation.
The real C-entry close test checks completion and snapshot detachment for its LSM
owner. Final receipt `close-store-accounting-preflight-v2` passes all 76 build
steps, 34 physical/WAL cases, 32 storage-read cases, 24 embedded close cases,
2 host close cases, 16 independently compiled archive cases and 45/1/8 identity
cases. There are no skips, failures or leaks. New cases reject all three original
errors at every accounting checkpoint with the data allocator exhausted, retain
reader ownership through begin/end/lifetime wait rejection, and retry cold legacy
arena accounting after observer-metadata allocation refusal. The fixtures cover
shared-account flat snapshots, unfrozen arenas, retirement queues and a sparse
bulk-account map; admitted totals match the full observer. Source/log hashes match
all 5,541 final inputs. The v1 receipt qualifies the initial scan and default
integration before the all-reader guard, sparse scan batching and cold-baseline
case.

Final status persistence still uses ordinary batch commit. Captured-input and
encoded/frozen WAL credit, manifest debt admission and the owning final status/WAL
state machine remain to be composed with this preflight and mutable publication.
The queued snapshot still needs admitted physical retirement alongside final
backend flush/retirement. Lite/object provider adoption and the complete default
pooling gate remain open; the full goal stays active and full GNU qualification
remains waived.
